articles.summary: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions
articles.keyPoints:
• Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions
• COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.
• The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy.

The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India can no longer afford its silence on the multi-trillion dollar AI arms race

The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. India’s AI policies are geared towards diffusion and research of helpful capabilities that can trickle down to the common citizen. The capabilities that the Union government and State governments seek to boost by leveraging AI are removed from the frontier research wreaking havoc within the information security profession around the world. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India’s focus on AI in international fora, such as the AI Impact Summit in Delhi, has been on consensus. This approach must change. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.
Editorial Context: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and administrative dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: U.S., China, Russia must draw up a roadmap for talks on nuclear weapons

The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: Will bank manager accept Kayalvizhi Alagiri’s apology, asks Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan grants a day’s time for the police to find out if the victim, subjected to physical assault, would agree for closure of criminal prosecution against the accused

The Madras High Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) wanted to know whether a bank manager would be willing to accept an apology from former Union Minister M.K. Alagiri’s daughter Kayalvizhi Alagiri and agree for closure of a criminal case registered against her for allegedly slapping him supposedly due to anger management issues on July 20, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan directed the Inspector of Shastri Nagar police station in Adyar, Chennai to make sure that Harsheen Singh, a branch manager with State Bank of India, appears before the court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) to explain if he is willing to accept the apology and give a quietus to the issue than continuing the prosecution.

The direction was issued during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by Ms. Alagiri seeking a direction to the police to register a First Information Report (FIR) against the bank manager on the basis of a counter complaint lodged by her on July 25, 2026 accusing him of having subjected her to verbal abuse, aggressive intimidation and public humiliation.

Government Advocate (criminal side) S. Yogaraja Sekar told the judge that Ms. Alagiri was the owner of a commercial building in which the bank branch was functioning. There was a dispute between the landlady and the tenant over the non-functioning of an elevator in the building and a quarrel over that issue had led to a physical assault against the bank manager on July 20, 2026.

The police had intially registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Ms. Alagiri under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abusing and assaulting the bank manager. It also completed the investigation and filed a charge sheet before a Metropolitan Magistrate in Chennai. The Magistrate was slated to take up the case for hearing next on December 22, 2026, the law officer said.

In so far as the counter complaint lodged by the landlady against the bank manager was concerned, the Government Advocate said, the police had conducted a preliminary inquiry but did not find any material to substantiate any of the allegations levelled by her. Therefore, the investigating officer had dropped further action and closed her complaint, he added.
On his part, the petitioner’s counsel S.L. Sudarsanam said, his client would apologise, if necessary and in order to give a quietus to the entire issue.

articles.title: CJP’s Saurav Das claims he was stopped at Delhi airport from travelling to U.K.
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In posts on X, Mr. Das said he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his 1 a.m. flight to London

Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convener Saurav Das on Monday (November 23, 2026) alleged that he was stopped from travelling to the U.K. to attend an event at the University of Oxford, where he was invited to speak on the "cockroach movement".
In posts on X, Mr. Das said he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport before boarding his 1 a.m. flight to London.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke alleged that someone in power was jealous of Mr. Das receiving an invitation from the University of Oxford.
Mr. Das said, "I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford."

"This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities like Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement.
"Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!" he said.
Mr. Das said he has been invited by the Oxford University Students' Union for a panel discussion.
"And that's why I was going to London. But as soon as I went to the immigration check, I came to know that my passport has been flagged," he said.
"Why is the government so scared of an educated youth going among educated people and having an intellectual discussion?
"I wish I was Nirav Modi. I wish I was Vijay Mallya. I wish I had looted thousands of crores from the banks..." he said.
🚨#ImportantAnnouncement🚨 I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford. @Cockroachisback
Taking a dig at the Modi government, the CJP leader said, "They are not even able to expand their cabinet because the ministers are refusing to resign."

articles.title: The Bilkis Bano order — justice deferred again
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The right to liberty cannot undermine a survivor’s dignity, voice and difficult quest for justice

“Justice is the first virtue of social institutions, as truth is of systems of thought,” said John Rawls in A Theory of Justice. The American political philosopher’s line is easy to admire yet hard to practice. When an institution cannot be trusted to hear a wronged person, the old maxim justice delayed is justice denied begins to sound less like a warning than a description.

For nearly a quarter of a century, Bilkis Bano, a survivor of the 2002 Gujarat riots who was gang-raped by 11 men while pregnant and lost some members of her family, has had to prove over and over again what happened to her was real, that it was a crime, and that the law should answer it. Each time, she has done so with a defiant courage that has become a testament to the Republic’s conscience. She now may have to do it again. On October 28, 2026, a Supreme Court Bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale suspended the life sentences of two of the 11 men convicted of gang-raping her and murdering some members of her family, granting them bail pending their appeals. Ms. Bano told the media that she learnt of the order just a few days ago through the press. The counsel for the two men later issued a statement on November 21, rejecting Ms. Bano’s allegation that she was kept in the dark about the proceedings but asserting that she was not party even in High Court.

“It is still baffling to me that for the second time after this order was passed, I have not been summoned to appear before the Supreme Court, nor has anything been heard from me,” Ms. Bano said in a statement through her attorneys. It is a sentence that no citizen, for whatever reason he may have for taking the oath regardless of his opinion of the merits of the order, should find easy to read.

Every word counts here. This case is designed to elicit both outrage and defensive responses. No one is found “not guilty” in the order. The principles, which were upheld by the Bombay High Court in 2017, remain the same. What the Bench has done is that it has merely suspended the sentences of the two men, Bipinchand Kanhaiyalal Joshi and Pradip Ramanlal Modhiya, until their appeals are disposed of, by pointing out that both men have been in jail for over 17 years, one of them has a severe disability, and their appeals raise questions of fact and law that require examination. The Additional Solicitor General opposed the pleas. The convicts’ appeals against the High Court’s judgment are still to be decided.

There is no objection to the order in the context of not subscribing to retributive or deterrent theories of punishment. However, at a time when there is talk of making the criminal justice system victim-centric, why was victimology forgotten in this case? That is the central question which survives despite the November 23, 2026 order by the same Bench releasing Siraj Pada, one of the convicts of the Sabarmati Express coach fire on similar grounds.

articles.title: Power outage during Minister’s programme in Kannur: KSEB staff rally behind suspended sub-engineer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Employees of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), under the banner of a joint action committee of officers and workers’ organisations, launched an agitation in Kannur on Monday (November 23) demanding the withdrawal of the suspension of sub-engineer Satheesh Babu in connection with a brief power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph on Saturday (November 21).

Hundreds of employees and officers from various KSEB offices joined the protest, with the organisations warning that the agitation would continue until the suspension was revoked. They also indicated that the protest could be extended across the State if the management failed to reconsider its decision.

The employees said the power supply had been disrupted for only about nine minutes as part of urgent maintenance work after a potentially dangerous fault was detected in an 11 kV feeder supplying the Kannur town area. They maintained that the interruption was necessary to avert a possible accident and that the required information had been communicated to consumers in advance through the outage management system and WhatsApp groups.

They alleged that neither the division office nor the section office had been informed about the Minister’s programme and that there was no question of deliberately disrupting the power supply. They also said that Mr. Babu had submitted an explanation when the authorities sought his response, but he was suspended without a proper preliminary inquiry.

Employees of the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB), under the banner of a joint action committee of officers and workers’ organisations, launched an agitation in Kannur on Monday (November 23) demanding the withdrawal of the suspension of sub-engineer Satheesh Babu in connection with a brief power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph on Saturday (November 21).

Hundreds of employees and officers from various KSEB offices joined the protest, with the organisations warning that the agitation would continue until the suspension was revoked. They also indicated that the protest could be extended across the State if the management failed to reconsider its decision.

The employees said the power supply had been disrupted for only about nine minutes as part of urgent maintenance work after a potentially dangerous fault was detected in an 11 kV feeder supplying the Kannur town area. They maintained that the interruption was necessary to avert a possible accident and that the required information had been communicated to consumers in advance through the outage management system and WhatsApp groups.

They alleged that neither the division office nor the section office had been informed about the Minister’s programme and that there was no question of deliberately disrupting the power supply. They also said that Mr. Babu had submitted an explanation when the authorities sought his response, but he was suspended without a proper preliminary inquiry.

The controversy erupted after the power disruption during the Electricity Minister’s programme at Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21. MLA T.O. Mohanan, who was present at the event, lodged a complaint with the KSEB chairman alleging deliberate disruption of the power supply. The suspension followed the complaint.

articles.title: Violence erupts in Pithapuram amid JSP councillors’ sparring over vice-chairman pick
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Jana Sena Party Councillors, supporters opposed the party’s decision to elect Bojja Venkateswara Rao as Pithapuram Municipal Vice-Chairman on the grounds of being a newcomer to the party.

Rift within the Jana Sena Party boiled over into open violence in Pithapuram on Monday as a bitter power struggle over the Municipal vice-chairman post culminated in the alleged assault of Veeramareddy Chakri, the personal assistant of JSP’s Kakinada MP Tangella Uday Srinivas, by party supporters.
In a purported video, JSP supporters are seen grabbing Mr. Chakri by his collar and repeatedly attacking him outside the Pithapuram municipal office.
The incident occurred when the MP was outside the municipal office, where JSP councillors raised slogans against his recommendation of Bojja Venkateswara Rao’s for the vice-chairman post.

However, a war of words among the JSP councillors began inside the municipal office when one councillor proposed Mr Venkateswara Rao’s name for the vice-chairman post, and the MP supported it. Of the 18 councillors who recently won in the local body polls, only six backed the move. Others disagreed with the choice, saying Mr Venkateswara Rao is a “newcomer” because he joined the party from the YSRCP after the 2024 general elections.

Later, JSP councillors proposed Pindi Sandhya’s name for the vice-chairman post. Senior party leader in the municipal council, Reddem Ramarao, rejected Mr. Venkateswara Rao’s candidature, claiming that the latter joined the party only after the 2024 general elections and that many senior leaders are eligible for the post. He backed Ms. Sandhya for the post.
Senior leader Pendem Dorababu and Mr. Uday Srinivas attempted to convince the party councillors, after which councillors withdrew their proposal for Ms. Sandhya as vice-chairperson.
“Venkateswara Rao has been elected as vice-chairman of Pithapuram Municipality unanimously,” Election Officer Sk. Mahaboob Sharif told The Hindu .
After the elections, JSP supporters have staged a dharna in front of Pithapuram municipal office, raising slogans against Mr. Uday Srinivas for offering the vice-chairman post to a newcomer.

Besides, JSP won 18 seats out of a total of 36 wards in Pithapuram municipality in Kakinada district; TDP won six seats while their partner BJP won a single seat in the recently concluded municipal election. However, as many as ten independent candidates, believed to be rebels of the NDA alliance, became councillors.

articles.title: Krushi OWS holds road safety awareness competitions for school students
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 250 students from various schools, including government schools in remote areas such as Paderu, participated in road safety awareness competitions organised by the Krushi Orthopaedic Welfare Society (Krushi OWS) at Alluri Seetharama Raju Vignana Kendram in the city on Sunday.

The programme featured painting, elocution, quiz, and short-film competitions to sensitise young people to road safety and the consequences of traffic accidents. Students from urban areas and distant places took part. Some of the short films highlighted the importance of wearing helmets and keeping tribal areas clean.

Dr. Kiran Kumar Nandivada, founder and CEO of Krushi OWS, orthopaedic spinal surgeon and rheumatologist, said the initiative aimed to create awareness about traffic violations and prevent accidents and disabilities. Founded in 1987, the society has been working for underprivileged people and persons with disabilities.

Recalling the severe injuries caused by road accidents, Dr. Kiran said such cases often required the involvement of several medical specialists and placed a considerable financial burden on families. He urged parents to discourage underage driving and guide children towards responsible road use.

The programme also showcased a video created using artificial intelligence by a visually impaired participant. Three Class VII students, two girls and a boy, who demonstrated knowledge of artificial intelligence, pledged to develop assistive devices for persons with disabilities.

articles.title: India, Finland seek to deepen economic ties through startup cooperation: Envoy Mikko Kivikoski
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: "We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mikki Kivikoski said

“India and Finland are looking to deepen economic cooperation by strengthening ties between their startup ecosystems and promoting greater two-way investment,” Finnish Ambassador to India Mikko Kivikoski has said.

"We want to engage more with the Indian startup actors. And of course, at the end of the day, this is all about advancing the economic cooperation between our countries. And here we see the startup sector, startup ecosystems, as an important part of that cooperation," Mr. Kivikoski told PTI .

The Ambassador was speaking at an unconventional startup event held at the Embassy of Finland in New Delhi on Friday (November 20, 2026), where entrepreneurs stepped into an ice-cold pool to pitch their ideas, drawing on Finland's winter-swimming tradition. "We have quite a long tradition in Finland for these kinds of events," Mr. Kivikoski said.

"This year has been record-high when it comes to interaction and engagement between Finland and India," he said, referring to visits by the Finnish Prime Minister and President, as well as meetings between the leaders of the two countries.

The Ambassador said the two sides agreed to elevate their bilateral relationship to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalisation and Sustainability during Finnish President Alexander Stubb's state visit to India in March.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met his Finnish counterpart, Petteri Orpo, in New Delhi on the sidelines of the AI Impact Summit in February and in Oslo on the margins of the 3rd India-Nordic Summit in May.

Mr. Kivikoski also referred to the visits to Finland by India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal during the summer. "We see India as a trusted partner when it comes to the Indo-Pacific area," he said.
The Ambassador said the India-Finland relationship was increasingly moving beyond conventional trade towards a partnership involving investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"What we are seeing already, and what is happening between the European Union and India and between India and Finland, is that we are now talking about partnership. It's not anymore about me selling something to you and you selling something to me," he said.

"There are more and more Finnish companies coming to the Indian market and more and more Indian companies going to the Finnish market. And of course we hope, and we are confident, that this dynamism will continue in the future," he said.

Bilateral trade in goods and services between India and Finland stood at around $3.7 billion in 2025-26, marking a growth of about 25% over the previous year, and a 38.5% rise from $2.64 billion in 2021-22.
The startup event, Polar Bear Pitching, originated in Oulu, northern Finland, and has expanded internationally, connecting startups with investors and business networks.

articles.title: A framework for nuclear risk reduction cannot wait
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Shenzhen offers an opening, but sustained engagement between Washington, Moscow and Beijing must now follow

For the first time since 1972, there is no treaty formally restricting the world’s largest nuclear arsenals. New START (New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty) expired in February, and nine months later, a successor treaty is still far from being drafted. Russia had offered to keep observing New START’s limits for a year if the United States did the same. Instead, the U.S. has pushed for an “improved” agreement, insisting that any nuclear treaty must involve China, which understandably has its own reservations.

On November 19, the leaders of the three countries met for the first time on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. They issued a joint declaration reaffirming that a nuclear war must never be fought. They also pledged subsequent talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. However, there are no provisions for the verification of compliance with these commitments, and no date seems to have been fixed for further talks. Despite Shenzhen, the underlying tension between the three countries’ positions remains. Each country’s position makes sense from where it sits, but at a time fraught with conflict, further complicated by emerging technologies, this treaty-less scenario cannot continue indefinitely.

Despite Shenzhen, the underlying tension between the three countries’ positions remains. Each country’s position makes sense from where it sits, but at a time fraught with conflict, further complicated by emerging technologies, this treaty-less scenario cannot continue indefinitely.

articles.title: Manik Saha says party probing presence of masked men in BJP election rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘I don’t support this. In fact, our party does not approve such behaviour from our ranks. The party is inquiring into the matter and will follow up,’ said Manik Saha

Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha on Monday (November 23, 2026) reacted to the presence of several masked youths in a BJP election rally in Agartala on Saturday (November 21). He said he had come to know this from newspaper reports and subsequently took up the matter with the party leadership.
“I don’t support this. In fact, our party does not approve such behaviour from our ranks. The party is inquiring into the matter and will follow up,” he told reporters.

Elections to 21 Urban Local Bodies including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) are due on November 27. The ruling BJP has already won five of them unopposed as candidates from other parties and independents did not submit nomination papers.

The appearance of several masked men at the BJP’s election rally in Agartala stirred controversy, with CPI(M) and Congress registering complaints to the state election commission. The Congress also lodged a complaint at the West Agartala Police Station.

Secretary of the State Election Commission on Monday (November 23) said they received complaints about the issues and forwarded them to the police headquarters for necessary action. He said the commission would ensure free and peaceful elections.

BJP sources said veteran minister and city campaign in-charge Ratan Lal Nath organised the procession. They said the masked youths were actually party supporters from Mohanpur, north of Agartala, home Assembly constituency of minister Nath.

CPI(M) and Congress, however, claimed the masked men were actually anti-socials who were likely to be engaged in creating trouble and rig the elections. They also complained of the silence of the police in initiating action despite registering complaints.
Tripura / Communist Party of India -Marxist / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Close to realising PM Narendra Modi’s dream for Kashmir, says Kiren Rijiju
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘I remember there were no large programmes as we visited frontier districts to meet soldiers and discuss how to realise the dream of PM Modi,’ said Kiren Rijiju

Terming the work of J&K Waqf Board as “the best-performing” in the country, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the region is close to achieve the dream Prime Minister Narendra Modi has for it.

Recalling his past tours of Kashmir as Minister of State (MOS) Home and as Law Minister, Mr. Rijiju said, “I remember there were no large programmes as we visited frontier districts to meet soldiers and discuss how to realise the dream of PM Modi. I must say we are very close to realising the dream PM Modi had for Kashmir. He set a goal not only for a peaceful region but also to take J&K to new heights,” said Mr. Rijiju, while speaking at the Waqf Day-2026 at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology in Srinagar.

Mr. Rijiju said Kashmir was moving ahead at a very “fast pace”. “Seeing the situation today, I can say India’s and J&K’s future is bright. People of Kashmir are large hearted. Today, sportsmen across the country wait to participate in the winter games at Gulmarg every year. The concept, besides adventure and water sports, was introduced in 2019,” said Mr. Rijiju.

Earlier in the day, the Union minister inaugurated the construction of Bibi Halima College of Nursing & Medical Technology (BHCNMT), at Kathi Darwaza, Rainawari, Srinagar. He said the alumni of the educational institute included 16 Kashmir University Gold Medalists, the highest among nursing colleges and over 10 international NCLEX qualifiers in the USA and Canada. “Its graduates also constitute around 30% of nursing officers at SKIMS and over 25% of the nursing workforce at Government Medical College-associated hospitals,” he added.

Praising the arrangements and management at the Nursing College and also the works done at the Hazratnal shrine, Mr. Rijiju said, “The space created at Hazratbal for female pilgrims to offer prayers is beautiful and aesthetically pleasing. I congratulate the Chairperson of the Waqf Board, Darakhshan Andrabi, in this regard. It’s the best performing board in the country.”

The Union Minister also highlighted the need to properly utilise and manage over nine lakh Waqf properties across the country. “It could bring significant socio-economic changes in the Muslim community. Poor and disadvantaged members of the Muslim community could benefit considerably if Waqf assets were utilised for their welfare, of which the J&K Waqf Board’s functioning is an example,” said Mr. Rijiju.
He also congratulated Ms. Andrabi and her entire team for “undertaking development initiatives and improving facilities at important religious and public institutions”.

Praising PM Modi for his vision. Mr. Andrabi said, “I became the first woman chairperson in 2022 and the board was constituted. There was no official structure then and the same was put in place. It is paying dividends.”

National Conference (NC) leader and Member of Parliament (MP) Mian Altaf highlighted the role of Mr. Rijiju pertaining to Kashmir. “He [Rijiju] frequently visits Kashmir and has always loved people. He always tried to contribute to Kashmir as he held different ministries. We all dream to have a better Kashmir, even what it was 30 years ago. My sister Ms. Andrabi is doing work that deserves applaud too,” said Mr. Altaf.
Jammu and Kashmir National Conference / national government / Narendra Modi

articles.title: Rajasthan women’s varsity signs MoU with BRICS nations for global leadership centre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Banasthali Vidyapith, a residential women’s university situated in Rajasthan’s Tonk district, on Monday (November 23, 2026) signed a memorandum of understanding with the BRICS nations for establishment of a centre for global women’s leadership. The new centre will work for women’s educational empowerment and leadership development on a global scale.

The MoU was signed on the conclusion of a five-day BRICS women leaders’ summit, organised on the university campus, which focused on promoting women’s leadership, cultural exchanges, and mutual cooperation and innovative research across the 11 BRICS member countries.

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla , who inaugurated the summit, called upon women leaders to harness their collective leadership, experience and innovative capabilities to address global challenges and shape a “more peaceful, stable and prosperous” world. He also laid emphasis on cooperation among BRICS nations.

Banasthali Vidyapith organised the summit in partnership with Eurasian Women’s Forum, Russia’s Federation Council, Senezh Management Group of Russia and BRICS Youth Alliance. Vice-Chancellor Ina Aditya Shastri said the participants would act as torchbearers for women’s leadership development in their respective countries.

Extensive discussions were held during the summit on developing women’s leadership in the fields of politics, higher education, science and technology, entrepreneurship, administration, and social development. The speakers agreed to formulate future action plans to address the challenges of inequality in opportunities, limited access to financial resources and socio-cultural barriers.

Senezh Management Workshop’s First Vice-Rector Sergey Vladimirovich Bocharov said the BRICS countries had much to learn from India and Banasthali Vidyapith’s model of women’s leadership. He said the new centre would help expand women’s role in civil society and strengthen their decision-making capacity.

articles.title: Proposal for extending scholarship to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical education in Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sri Lankan Deputy High Commission (SLDHC) in Chennai is proposing to strengthen cooperation in medical education in Tamil Nadu, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students. Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran met Health Minister K.G. Arunraj in this regard recently.

“During the meeting, discussion focused on further strengthening cooperation in the field of medical education, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical studies in Tamil Nadu under a proposed 50/50 scholarship between the government of Tamil Nadu and the university concerned,” SLDHC said in a social media post.

Mr. Geathiswaran meeting with the Minister last week also explored the potential for establishing student exchange programmes for medical students and postgraduate trainees, including opportunities for clinical rotations, academic exchanges and professional engagement between medical institutions in Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu, it said.

National & Polity Report: Proposal for extending scholarship to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical education in Tamil Nadu. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and administrative governance framework.

Institutional Framework: The update directly connects with parliamentary procedures, centre-state relations under the Seventh Schedule, and constitutional bodies responsible for upholding statutory mandates.

articles.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Each previous instance coincided with extraordinary disruptions, from the Emergency and Lok Sabha dissolutions to Indira Gandhi’s assassination and the COVID-19 pandemic

The Winter Session of Parliament has been skipped only four times in India’s parliamentary history, and each instance was linked to exceptional circumstances, including the Emergency, the premature dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

With the Monsoon Session yet to be prorogued, setting a record for Parliament remaining unprorogued for more than 100 days, speculation has grown over the possibility of a short special session to consider the delimitation Bill.

articles.title: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump path to erasing hush money conviction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court; if that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity

A federal appeals court on Monday (November 23, 2026) gave U.S. President Donald Trump a new pathway to erasing his hush money criminal conviction, moving the case to a federal court where he could seek to have it dismissed on immunity grounds.

A three-judge panel of the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision that had kept the case in state court in New York, where Mr. Trump was tried and convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.

The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court. If that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity.

The decision also set in motion a halt to proceedings in Mr. Trump's simultaneous state court appeal. Trump denies wrongdoing and was given no punishment in the case, which made him the first U.S. President convicted of a crime.

In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein's earlier denial of Mr. Trump's request to move the historic case from state court to federal court, a process known as removal.

articles.title: LoP Ritabrata Banerjee files counter complaint against Mamata-Trinamool for fabrication of signature on affidavits
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Both Trinamool factions raise allegations of signature forgery and document fabrication, file complaints against each other

Leader of Opposition in West Bengal Ritabrata Banerjee on Monday (November 23, 2026) filed a police complaint against Mamata-All India Trinamool Congress for fabricating signatures on affidavits to claim their stake in the party name and symbol. A day earlier, Mamata-Trinamool filed a complaint against Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee under similar allegations.
The Democratic Trinamool Congress MLA, along with Opposition chief whip Akhruzamman and spokesperson Riju Dutta went to the Kalighat Police Station to file the complaint.

“They have threatened many people to sign affidavits; they also manipulated a few MLAs to sign under false pretense. We have already filed complaints at various police stations. We will share them with the ECI,” Mr Ritabrata Banerjee said. He also added that people have been made to sign affidavits under false claims of filling up forms for various schemes, relief materials, and other things and that it was an attempt to “mislead” people.

Since the regime change in West Bengal, the Trinamool Congress has bifurcated into two factions, with almost 65 of 80 Trinamool MLAs rallying behind Mr Ritabrata Banerjee and abandoning the Mamata Banerjee faction. As tensions rose, both factions exercised their claims over the party’s name and symbol. However, Election Commission of India (ECI) barred both from using the original “All India Trinamool Congress” name and the party symbol.
Since the split, both factions have submitted an array of affidavits with the ECI in support of each of the faction’s claim over the symbol and party name.

Mamata-Trinamool leader Subhasish Chakraborty had filed the official complaint dated November 20, against Mr Ritabrata Banerjee at the same Kalighat Police Station for falsification, forging signatures of unsuspecting citizens and creation and fabrication of affidavits which have allegedly been filed before the ECI.
In the complaint filed by Mamata-Trinamool, they have also named Nanoor Police Station Officer-in-charge Sanjoy Sarkar, MLA Arup Roy, and several others as co-conspirators in the case.

“The material and evidence presently in my possession disclose that an organised exercise has been undertaken through the machinery of Nanoor Police Station for the preparation of fake affidavits in support of the rival faction, including affidavits purporting to show that ordinary members of the public recognise Arup Roy as the leader of the AITC and do not accept Smt. Mamata Banerjee as its leader,” reads the copy of the police complaint.

This comes after Mamata-AITC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had earlier on November 5 claimed that he has video evidence of fabricated affidavits being filed out in favour of Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee.

“He says one thing in the morning, another in the evening and something else at night. Answering his questions is a waste of time and energy. I don’t have that much time,” Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee said on Monday (November 23).
West Bengal / All India Trinamool Congress / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Chinese neuroscientist at Princeton is held by ICE after detention at Washington airport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘News of Eva’s detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,’ Rodney Priestley, dean of the university’s graduate school, said in a statement

A Chinese neuroscience researcher at Princeton University is in the custody of immigration authorities after she was detained while trying to get on a flight back from Washington, marking another instance of federal enforcement at airports.

Eva Yi Xie, a third-year doctoral student at Princeton, was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Thursday (November 19, 2026) as she tried to fly back to New Jersey from a conference in the nation's capital, her university adviser Carlos Brody said in a social media post.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, says Ms. Xie overstayed her visa and did not have authorisation to study in the United States.

“News of Eva's detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,” Rodney Priestley, dean of the university's graduate school, said in a statement. "We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton.”

Two days after Ms. Xie was taken into custody in Washington, masked immigration officers detained a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge in Seattle. ICE has ramped up detentions at airports since the summer, especially targeting people it says have overstayed their visas.

Kerry Doyle, Ms. Xie's lawyer, said she came to the U.S. at age 14 with her family from China and has had an asylum application pending for years. Mr. Doyle insisted that Ms. Xie has permission to live, work and study in the U.S. while her case is pending.
Mr. Doyle said Ms. Xie is being held in ICE's Caroline Detention Centre in Virginia.

DHS said in a statement that Ms. Xie came to the United States on a temporary visa on March 16, 2016, but “chose to violate our nation's laws by refusing to depart by the required date of September 15, 2016.”
The agency said she did not have valid permission to study in the U.S. and “a pending application does not confer legal status.”
“Xie will receive due process and remain in ICE custody pending her removal proceedings," the DHS statement said.

Democratic Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey said in a statement that his office contacted ICE and didn't get a “satisfactory response” about why she was detained. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, also a Democrat, directed her administration to coordinate with federal lawmakers and the state of Virginia to get more information.

“While ICE claims to go after the worst of the worst, time and again the record shows they do not -- and their tactics are making New Jerseyans less safe,” Ms. Sherrill's spokesperson, Steve Sigmund, said in an email.

articles.title: Sanjay Raut accuses State Assembly Speaker Rahul Narwekar of tribal land grab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sanjay Raut has demanded to register a criminal case under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act

Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut on Monday (November 23, 2026) has requested Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to order an independent investigation into allegations accusing state assembly speaker Rahul Narwekar and his associates of illegally encroaching on land, evicting Katkari tribal families from their homes in Maharashtra’s Raigad district. Mr. Narwekar has dismissed the allegations, calling it “baseless”.

Mr. Raut has written a letter to Mr. Fadnavis, raising concerns around displacement of Katkari tribal community from Mhatroli village in Raigad district’s Alibaug taluka. He has asked Mr. Fadnavis to rehabilitate them on their original land or an alternative site with compensation.

In a letter dated November 22, Mr. Raut stated, “On 20 March 2025, in the middle of the night, 20 Adivasi families were displaced by forcibly evicting them with a bulldozer. The 15-acre plot was purchased in 2017 by Rahul Narvekar in the name of his wife Sarita Rahul Narvekar.”
Mr. Raut has demanded to register a criminal case under the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
Mr. Narwekar threatened to file a defamation suit, saying, “Mr. Raut has made baseless allegations, and the mentioned plot is lawfully purchased property after the title disputes had been settled.”
Maharashtra / Mumbai / Shiv Sena-Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray

articles.title: Seven-member committee appointed to frame air ambulance SOPs
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik said that the State government has directed the committee to submit its report within two months from the date of the Government Resolution
Maharashtra government has set up a seven-member committee to frame a standard operating procedure for air ambulances and new ambulances operating across the State.

Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik on Monday (November 23, 2026) said that the State government has directed the committee to submit its report within two months from the date of the Government Resolution.

The GR was issued on Monday (November 23, 2026), mentioning that the Additional Transport Commissioner Ravi Gaikwad will head the panel with officials from the transport, public health, and police departments.

The GR comes after the October 13 meeting, where Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik and Public Health Minister Prakash Abitkar decided to prepare a separate SOP for air ambulances and new ambulance services in Maharashtra.
Following the meeting, directions were given through the Transport Commissioner’s office to constitute a committee to prepare the SOP.

In October, the State government decided to launch an air ambulance service on three major highways of the state from next year, including Samruddhi Mahamarg (Mumbai-Nagpur highway), Pune-Mumbai Expressway and Mumbai-Goa highway. The State government was eyeing to complete the SOPs by November 15.

The other members of the team are Additional Commissioner of Police (Traffic) Mokshada Patil, Superintendent of Police from the office of the Additional Director General of Police (Traffic) Sunil Bhardwaj, Deputy Secretary of the Public Health Department Rajshree Sarang, Deputy Director Jayant Mule, and Police Deputy Superintendent of the Road Safety Cell of the Transport Commissioner’s office Pramod Tawde. Deputy Transport Commissioner of the Road Safety Cell of the Transport Commissioner’s office, Sachinkumar Giri, will work as the Member-Secretary of the committee.

articles.title: Nagpur Bench grants parole to prisoner for marriage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A division bench comprising Justices Urmila Joshi-Phalke and Raj D. Wankhede dismissed the objections raised by the State administration

The Nagpur Bench of the Court of Judicature at Bombay has ruled that an individual incarcerated in a facility can be granted release for a duration to marry, overturning a decision by authorities that cited the absence of a provision in the Rules of 2024 for Prisons in Maharashtra regarding furlough and parole for the event, and stating that a denial based on the ground does not stand.
A division bench comprising Justices Urmila Joshi-Phalke and Raj D. Wankhede dismissed the objections raised by the State administration.

It clarified that the provision regarding marriage under Rule 12(3) of the regulations applies to the marriage of the individual incarcerated, and observed that there is no connection between a requirement to spend a duration of one year in custody and the grounds for granting release on parole. It also took note of an order issued previously which had declared a condition under Rule 14 regarding a duration of one year as a violation of Article 14 and Article 21 of the Constitution, and subsequently cancelled the order of rejection issued by an official at the facility and granted release on parole for a duration of seven days.

The matter pertains to an individual named Kunal alias Golu Anil Jaiswal, who is undergoing a sentence of imprisonment for the duration of life at a facility located in Morshi within the jurisdiction of Amravati district. He had approached the court after an official holding the post of Deputy Superintendent at the facility rejected his application on July 7, 2026, citing the absence of a provision in the rules for release on parole for the marriage of the applicant, despite a report from officers of the police following a check of records favoring the request for an event scheduled to take place in Nagpur on December 4, 2026.

The State administration had relied upon Rule 12(3) to argue that while release on parole is permissible for the marriage of children and relatives of the individual in custody, there exists no provision for the marriage of the applicant, and had further contended that release on parole cannot be granted again if an individual has availed the benefit and has not completed a duration of one year.

The order grants release for a duration of seven days, during which the individual is required to mark presence at a station of the police in Nagpur from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. on December 4, and is directed to surrender before the authority at the facility in Morshi on day eight of the period.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh polls: SP, Congress kick off seat-sharing talks
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The meeting held at the residence of Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari in New Delhi lasted just about 20 minutes, and the two sides are likely meet again November 24 to take the negotiations forward

The first round of seat-sharing talks between the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections started in New Delhi on Monday (November 23, 2026), with leaders from both parties indicating that an alliance deal could be finalised soon.

The meeting held at the residence of Congress Rajya Sabha MP Pramod Tiwari in New Delhi lasted just about 20 minutes, and the two sides are likely meet again on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) to take the negotiations forward.
Samajwadi Party National General Secretary and Rajya Sabha MP Ram Gopal Yadav, who is leading the SP team, said the discussions were held in a cordial atmosphere.

“The meeting took place in a very cordial atmosphere. We listened to each other’s points of view, and we will soon finalise this alliance and inform you about it,” he told reporters after the meeting.
Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam also said that both parties trust each other and will manage things jointly.
Sources have indicated that it is the first round of discussions, and the alliance will take time to reach an agreement on 403 assembly seats.
A Congress leader who was part of the negotiations said on condition of anonymity that the Congress shared a list of around 130 seats that it wants to contest in the alliance with the SP.

“We have shared our list of preferred seats. It is around 130-odd seats. We have done a detailed survey and the demand is based on the outcome of 2024 Lok Sabha polls and our performance in previous assembly elections,” he said.

“In the assembly segments coming under six Lok Sabha seats we won in 2024, we are very strong. The discussions will continue. Our broader objective is to defeat the authoritarian Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) regime, but our approach in selection of seats is evidence and data-based,” added the leader.
In the evening, a parallel meeting of the Congress party was under way, in which they discussed the response of the SP and how to move forward.
Sunil Singh Yadav ‘Sajan’, the SP spokesperson, said winnability will be sole criteria to decide which party will contest a particular seat.

“Winnability will be sole criteria to decide which seat a party will contest in the 2027 polls. There is a broader understanding between our leader Akhilesh ji and Congress leader Rahul ji about defeating the BJP. In our alliance, we are partners and we will collectively defeat the BJP,” said Mr. Sajan.

articles.title: What stands atop Thiruparankundram hill is a survey pillar, ascertains Tamil Nadu government report
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: This report has evoked interest against the backdrop of the latest dispute over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam atop Thiruparankundram hill, which has taken centre stage, following the Supreme Court’s decision to permit the lighting of the lamp at the newly identified deepathoon as a limited, one-time arrangement

A 2026 report compiled by the Departments of Survey and Settlement and Archaeology of the Tamil Nadu government ascertains that the pillar near the Sikandar Badusha Dargah in Thirupparankundram hill is a Great Trigonometrical Survey (GTS) pillar erected by the British. The map prepared by the Departments identifies the original Deepathoon (lamp pillar) to be below the dargah.

This report has evoked interest against the backdrop of the latest dispute over the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam atop Thiruparankundram hill has taken centre stage, following the Supreme Court’s decision to permit the lighting of the lamp at the newly identified deepathoon as a limited, one-time arrangement.

The report says the triangulation bearings from Sikandarmalai hill station (Tiruparankundrum) to other stations such as Nagamalai, Sadragiri, Gopalswami, Kutiparai, Madurai temple (Meenakshi Amman temple), Ponurikimalai and Perumalmalai, taken in the present survey, are consistent with values given in the GTS report of the colonial period.

Great Trigonometrical Survey location with pillar and the Deepam pillar (Deepathoon) with inscription located at the lower point on the Sikandarmalai hill (Thirupparankundram). | Photo Credit: Tamil Nadu Departments of Survey and Settlement and Archaeology

“These values suggest that the pillar installed at Sikandarmalai and the associated station marks engraved in situ on the rocky surface having circle with a dot is a survey pillar,” says the report prepared by officials from the Survey and Settlement and Archaeology Departments.

In the five-volume report, running over 1,800 pages, more than 800 stations were identified in the survey’s first phase. Of these, 484 stations, comprising 210 primary and 274 secondary stations, were physically documented. Thirupparankundram was a secondary station with stone pillar and stone mark.

The Great Trigonometrical Survey station (pillar) and the control points forming a triangle at Sikandarmalai hill (Thirupparankundram). | Photo Credit: Tamil Nadu Departments of Survey and Settlement and Archaeology

The report was based on the order issued by the Revenue and Disaster Management Department of Tamil Nadu in December 2025, to systematically identify and document all GTS stations. In August, 2026, the Revenue Department granted permission to publish the report. The Department of Survey and Settlement comes under the administrative control of the Revenue and Disaster Management Department.
The Government Order issued by the Tamil Nadu Revenue Department in December 2025, to systematically identify and document all GTS stations. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

In the Survey, stations were established through triangulation, which involves measuring angles between contiguous points relative to a baseline. Landscapes with hills provided clear lines of sight, making it easier to fix triangulation points, whereas flat areas required more stations due to limited visibility.

The order says that historically, survey stations and control points were meticulously marked on GTS maps, topo sheets, and village maps, and served as anchors for cartography and land management. However, the passage of time, coupled with rapid and often unplanned urbanisation, terrain change due to natural calamities, extensive industrialisation, and unfortunately, instances of human vandalism, rendered many of these original physical station points untraceable.

According to the order, the Director of Survey and Settlement proposed to undertake a comprehensive field exercise to systematically identify, map, document, and preserve all GTS stations in Tamil Nadu, and to use their coordinates to conduct subsequent surveys in the State.

articles.title: India, China hold 10-day talks to ease LAC tensions in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The talks focused on establishing engagement protocols, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, and maintaining open communication channels

India and China have concluded a second round of Corps Commander-level talks aimed at easing tensions along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh and putting in place measures to prevent friction between troops deployed along the frontier ahead of the onset of harsh winter conditions.

Sources in the Ministry of Defence confirmed that the closely guarded discussions, which began on November 8, 2026, a day after Deepavali, continued for nearly 10 days, with a short break in between. The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully.

Lieutenant-General Girish Kalia, General Officer Commanding of the Army’s III Corps, also known as the Spear Corps, led the Indian delegation. The formation is headquartered at Rangapahar near Dimapur in Nagaland. His Chinese counterpart and other military officers participated in the discussions. An official from the Ministry of External Affairs was also present.

The latest round of talks primarily focused on establishing engagement protocols between the two sides, preventing face-offs and misunderstandings between troops deployed along the frontier, maintaining open communication channels and reducing tensions in the eastern sector. Both countries have deployed substantial numbers of troops in the region.

The discussions assume significance as winter conditions along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh can become extremely severe, posing considerable challenges to troop sustenance, movement and logistical support. Any delay in implementing the measures discussed could complicate the situation on the ground as temperatures fall and access to forward areas becomes increasingly difficult.

The second round follows the first Corps Commander-level meeting, held on September 6 and 7, 2026, at the Wacha-Damai Border Personnel Meeting (BPM) point in the Kibithoo sector. Wacha is India’s easternmost border personnel meeting point.
The first meeting was convened following reports of tensions in the Taksing area of Upper Subansiri district in Arunachal Pradesh, where troops from the two sides had reportedly come face to face.

The military-level engagement comes amid renewed diplomatic efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations. In August 2026, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, the Special Representatives for boundary negotiations between the two countries, held talks in Beijing.

The situation along the Arunachal Pradesh frontier also came into focus in October 2026, when Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) Director-General Shatrujeet Kapur, days before his retirement, said Indian and Chinese troops had faced off at multiple locations in the State.

articles.title: Vance, Rubio meet with Qatari PM as uncertainty mounts over Trump's intentions with Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The development comes after Donald Trump told Mr. Vance that the administration did not need a deal with Iran and instructed him to focus on fraud and crime in Democratic-led cities following the Republican Party's wipeout in this month's midterm election

U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio met on Monday (November 23, 2026) separately with the Prime Minister of Qatar, the Gulf country that has played a key role in efforts to revive stalled negotiations on ending the U.S. conflict with Iran.

Mr. Vance held talks with Qatar's Prime Minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, at the White House, according to a person familiar with the meeting. The person, who spoke on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the discussions, would not give details of the meeting.
The Vice President's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The development comes after President Donald Trump told Mr. Vance that the administration did not need a deal with Iran and instructed him to focus on fraud and crime in Democratic-led cities following the Republican Party's wipeout in this month's midterm elections . The Vice President, who had been the chief negotiator on a brief ceasefire agreement, has blamed voter unhappiness with the Iran war for the Republican losses.

Mr. Trump has left much of the world guessing about his next moves in the nearly nine-month-old conflict, with fears growing among U.S. allies in the region about the possible resumption of all-out war.

Even as both sides carry out sporadic bursts of military action, Mr. Trump has said he does not see the need to resume major operations. But the U.S. has maintained a naval blockade on Iranian shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a crucial waterway for the global energy trade.

Mr. Trump said at a news conference Friday at the White House that Tehran wants an agreement to end hostilities but not one that is “acceptable” to him, insisting that “we want to make a real deal, not a fake deal.”

Mediators have been pushing proposals that would aim to lift disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for limited sanctions relief for Iran and paving the way for a resumption in broader negotiations to include Tehran's nuclear program.

Qatar's Prime Minister was visiting Washington for a biannual meeting of the U.S.-Qatar Strategic Dialogue with Mr. Rubio. The dialogue encompasses a broad range of regional security issues, including Iran, as well as relations between Washington and Doha.

The State Department said after the meeting that Mr. Rubio had “expressed appreciation for Qatar's global mediation efforts and stressed the importance of continued close coordination to deter threats and promote stability and security across the Middle East.”

A joint statement said the strategic dialogue involved discussions of “shared policy priorities” ranging from the West Asia to Africa and Latin America, but it did not reveal any new policy directions or priorities.
“We're working together to advance shared economic and security priorities and strengthen our partnership to promote a more stable and secure Middle East,” Mr. Rubio posted on X.

articles.title: Trump orders U.S. Army to pause detonation of lead explosives in Iowa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. appeals court lifts previous stay that blocked detonation; opponents raise concerns about toxic lead dust cloud

U.S. President Donald Trump ordered ‌the Army on Monday (November 23, 2026) to hold off on its plan to blow up a deteriorating ​stockpile of toxic lead explosives in rural Iowa, saying it should be up ⁠to the courts and the State’s Governor-elect to decide whether to allow the detonation.

Hours later, the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals gave judicial clearance for the detonation plan, lifting a stay the court issued Thursday temporarily freezing ‌an Environmental Protection Agency permit for the demolition.

The Army stirred a public outcry last week when details surfaced of its ‌plan to detonate 68 storage drums, or nearly 10,000 pounds (4,500 kilograms), of degraded lead azide, ‌an explosive ⁠chemical used in military munitions, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa.

An aerial view shows homes on November 20, 2026 in Middletown, Iowa. The town, which sits on the edge of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, faced evacuations because the Army was planning to detonate of several tons of highly-volatile lead azide at the facility. | Photo Credit: Getty Images via AFP

Environmental ⁠groups challenging the Army’s disposal plan in court have raised public safety concerns over the likelihood that the explosion would release a plume of toxic lead dust over homes, crops and livestock far beyond the detonation site.

The EPA has countered ​that a managed detonation would be far less ‌risky than an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion of the dangerously unstable material, a scenario the agency said was growing more likely as the weather turns colder in Iowa. According to the EPA, any attempt to relocate the storage drums would likewise risk spontaneous explosion.

Writing on his Truth Social platform ‌on Monday, Mr. Trump said he believed “the proper course” was for the Army to proceed ​with the controlled detonation. But the Republican president added that he has “ordered the military not to do so until such time as the Eighth Circuit agrees that we ⁠can go forward.”
He also said Iowa’s Democratic governor-elect, Rob Sand, should approve any such decision. Mr. Sand does not take office until January so lacks authority to act until then.

Mr. Sand posted a ‌statement on X kicking the issue back to Mr. Trump, saying, “The Administration should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks.”
The Governor-elect wrote on Sunday that “no good options exist” and called for “transparency over how we got here.”

The current Governor, Republican Kim Reynolds, on Sunday said she had activated Iowa’s emergency operations centre to better coordinate between State and Federal agencies, including the Army, ‌EPA and U.S. Department of Agriculture.

“While the detonation is a federal operation, it’s important for the state to be ​engaged in the preparation process so we can support the work of our federal partners in responding to the needs of Iowans,” Ms. Reynolds said. “Protecting the health and safety of ⁠our people and communities is our highest priority.”
