articles.title: Expanded NCD survey in Andhra Pradesh to cover four additional health conditions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In addition to the existing five major conditions, obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders are now a part of the exercise conducted every financial year

The Department of Health, Medical and Family Welfare has announced that health screenings being conducted in the State under the Non-Communicable Diseases (NCD) survey will be expanded to cover four additional health conditions — obesity, fatty liver disease, chronic respiratory conditions and mental health disorders.
Until now, screening has been conducted for people aged 18 and above for five major health conditions — hypertension, diabetes, oral cancer, breast cancer and cervical cancer.
The health screenings will be conducted every financial year, and the survey for the financial year 2026–27 is expected to begin soon.
“The programme is being expanded, considering changing lifestyles, rising obesity levels and growing risk of other chronic diseases,” a release from the department said on Tuesday.

Participating in a virtual review meeting on the upcoming NCD programme, Health Minister Satya Kumar Yadav briefed officials on the proposed changes and the precautions to be taken. “The focus is on identifying these diseases at an early stage before the problem becomes a serious one,” he said.

Under the new survey, individuals who are overweight will be identified at an early stage, and their risk of developing other health complications will be assessed. They will also receive guidance on dietary habits, physical activity and weight management. People with obesity, hypertension, diabetes and thyroid disorders will also be assessed for their risk of developing fatty liver disease.

The survey will also identify those with chronic respiratory conditions at an early stage. Those with symptoms will be examined by medical officers at the Primary Health Centres (PHCs). Patients requiring further investigations will be referred to the regional and district hospitals, where spirometers will be made available to assess lung function.

To assess the mental health condition of an individual, a questionnaire will be prepared, which will include questions to identify symptoms of depression, anxiety, memory-related problems and psychotic disorders.

Individuals identified as being at risk will undergo preliminary telephonic assessments through Tele-MANAS. Those requiring further medical evaluation will be referred to the appropriate healthcare facilities through the District Mental Health Programme.

The Minister directed the officials to adopt a Facial Recognition System (FRS)-based identification mechanism during the upcoming survey, which means biometric details would be collected during the survey for verification.

An Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA) ID would be generated for individuals, and their medical records linked to it. Details of screenings, disease diagnosis, treatment and follow-up consultations would be digitally recorded.

articles.title: Lula draws the line amid Trump interference in Brazil’s close and tough election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Lula says ‘Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard’ even as the country’s top intelligence agency raises the risk of U.S. interference in the October 4 elections to a ‘critical level’. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs and sanctions

In an unprecedented move last Wednesday (September 23, 2026), Brazilian President Lula da Silva’s campaign asked the country’s Federal Supreme Court (STF) to “investigate the possible U.S. interference in the country’s electoral process”. Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) also filed a case with the Superior Election Tribunal (TSE) against the far-right presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, seeking a probe into alleged U.S. support for his campaign.

The petitions came the same day as 14 countries belonging to the Shield of the Americas, a group of right-wing Latin American governments assembled by U.S. President Donald Trump, signed a pact designating 24 drug-trafficking groups as “shared threats”. Brazil’s two criminal organisations, First Capital Command (PCC) and Red Command (CV), were among the groups mentioned in the deal. Lula immediately hit back at the decision. “Brazil does not underestimate the challenge posed by organized crime, but it does not intend to outsource the responsibility of protecting its citizens,” the Brazilian leader said in his speech at the United Nations.

In his UN speech, Lula minced no words about how the U.S. threat is being perceived in Brazil. “In Latin America and the Caribbean, geographical proximity to the world’s greatest military power is inescapable… But Brazil does not fit in anyone’s backyard,” Lula declared to loud applause. The Brazilian did not meet Mr. Trump in New York; instead, he engaged with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Senator Bernie Sanders, in what was seen as a political message to Mr. Trump.

Brazil goes to the polls on October 4 in a tense election. Lula leads Mr. Flávio by five points in the first-round polls. If they meet again in the second round on October 25, polls show a close race, adding to fears of U.S. interference influencing the result. In recent months, the Trump administration has put enormous pressure on Brazil through tariffs , sanctions and by classifying PCC and CV as terrorist organisations.

Adding to the concerns is a confidential report sent recently by Brazil’s Intelligence Agency (Abin) to the President and TSE. The report raised the risk of U.S. interference to a “critical level”. The Abin assessment, reported widely by the Brazilian media, says the “reaffirmation of U.S. hegemony” in Latin America is a priority for Washington, particularly to counter China’s influence over strategic assets.

articles.title: China announces shock corruption probe into Politburo member
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining was earlier expected to assume a top leadership role in 2027

A prominent Chinese politician who is a member of the ruling Communist Party of China’s Politburo and was widely tipped for a top national leadership position in 2027 was placed under a shock disciplinary investigation on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The surprising announcement of “suspected severe violations” by Chen Jining, who has since 2022 been the top CPC leader in Shanghai and has served on the 25-member Politburo, left political observers in Beijing stunned.

Mr. Chen (62) was tipped to take on a prominent national role in the once-in-five-year Party Congress set for next year, which will see a major reshuffle. President Xi Jinping is expected to begin a fourth term in 2027.

Mr. Chen “is being investigated by the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision for suspected severe violations of discipline and laws,” a brief statement said.

Mr. Chen was previously the president of Mr. Xi’s alma mater, Tsinghua University, and served as the mayor of Beijing between 2018 and 2022, before his promotion to the Politburo as the Party Secretary of China’s financial centre, Shanghai.

In Shanghai, Mr. Chen was popular with foreign business representatives and is among the few leaders in the top echelons of the CPC with significant international exposure, having conducted his doctoral studies in environmental engineering at Imperial College London.

Politburo members are rarely investigated, and only half a dozen Politburo-level members in the last three decades have been removed. Notably, removals have often coincided with the run-up to Party Congresses that see leadership promotions and reshuffles.

Another former Shanghai Party Secretary, Chen Liangyu, was removed in 2006, a year before the 2007 Congress that saw the anointment of Mr. Xi as former leader Hu Jintao’s successor. The year of Mr. Xi’s ascension in 2012 saw the removal of Bo Xilai, then Party Secretary in Chongqing.

Under Mr. Xi, two Politburo-ranked members have been removed, including the former security chief Zhou Yongkang who retired from the Politburo Standing Committee, the party’s highest body, in 2012 and was placed under investigation in 2014. Another former Chongqing Party Secretary, Sun Zhengcai, was removed in 2017. Mr. Chen will likely be the third.

Mr. Chen was present at the CPC’s Fifth Plenum in Beijing last month, a key annual meeting that confirmed the expulsion of as many as 33 members of the party’s Central Committee, including 16 PLA Generals, and concluded with a pledge to “persevere with full and rigorous party self-governance”.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Panel, headed by TISS director, calls for task force and special courts to deal with leak cases, the creation of a body to manage exam venues, third-party audits, cyber security measures, and monitoring devices

People involved in leaking recruitment examination papers should be punished with a fine of ₹10 crore and life imprisonment, according to the recommendations of a committee set up by the Maharashtra government, which submitted its report on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The panel, headed by the director of the Tata Institute of Social Sciences, also proposed a framework to oversee the process of conducting tests, including a third party audit and a new body to manage exam venues.

This committee was set up in the wake of a paper leak in an examination to recruit pharmacists and drug inspectors for 954 posts, conducted by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission on March 22. It was later discovered that the paper had already been leaked on WhatsApp, leading to the cancellation of the recruitment process on August 25, and an investigation into the matter. The State government set up the committee on September 4, after candidates sought a review of the exam process to recommend changes in the system.

Apart from a recommended penalty of a ₹10 crore fine and life imprisonment for individuals involved in paper leaks, the panel called for the establishment of a task force to address leak incidents, courts for the disposal of cases, and a body to manage exam venues, to bring accountability to district officials and prevent such leaks.

The panel proposes a third party audit, a cyber security cell, surveillance cameras, and signal-blocking devices at venues. Police personnel should be appointed to the Commission’s teams and non-governmental institutions need to be monitored to reduce irregularities in the selection of venues, the committee said. It also called for the publication of statistics regarding vacant posts and the development of a portal to resolve issues faced by candidates.

With regard to the pharmacist selection exam, the report recommends a fee refund by the Maharashtra Public Service Commission for all candidates who file income tax returns. The panel also suggested an increase in the number of posts for the Group-C exam, an extra attempt for candidates, an exam schedule to be announced by October, and a grievance portal to ensure transparency.

articles.title: KSEB revokes suspension of engineer over power disruption during Minister’s programme in Kannur
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) has revoked the suspension of Satheesh Babu P.V., a sub-engineer attached to the Kannur electrical section. He was suspended following a power disruption during a programme attended by Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph at the Jawahar Library Hall in Kannur on November 21.

The suspension was withdrawn through an order issued by the executive engineer on Tuesday (November 24), following a review of the circumstances surrounding the incident and the report submitted by senior officials. Mr. Babu had been suspended pending inquiry after power supply was disrupted during the Minister’s programme on the morning of November 21.
The decision to reconsider the suspension followed a direction from the Deputy Chief Engineer, Electrical Circle, Kannur, on November 23.
In his report, the assistant executive engineer said that the official was unaware of the programme attended by the Minister and had intended to carry out routine maintenance work.
The suspension had triggered protests from KSEB employees’ organisations.

articles.title: Demand gets louder for restrictions on nightlife at Kozhikode beach
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Kuttichira residents urge the district administration and the police to restrict activities at Kozhikode beach and in their neighbourhood from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

Nightlife at the Kozhikode beach and surrounding areas, one of the major tourist attractions in the city, is in the news, with residents seeking restrictions on people’s activities there in view of the reported involvement of anti-social elements.

District Collector M.S. Madhavikutty and District Police Chief (Kozhikode City) A.P. Shoukathali conducted a surprise inspection of the stretch from the South Beach to Konnad Beach on November 21. They were accompanied by officials from the departments of Port, Fisheries, and Health, and those from the district tourism promotion council and the Kozhikode Corporation. In view of a special branch report citing safety concerns, the officials examined complaints related to a lack of proper lighting in the area, broken tiles, disposal of waste, and the management of wastewater from the Food Street on the beach.

The special branch had reportedly said that restrictions could be imposed in places that lacked proper lighting and security arrangements. Though the stretch from the open stage to Mukhadar beach is relatively secure, areas such as Butt Road, Kothi beach, and Konnad beach are in a pitiable condition. The suggestion is to restrict the entry of people into these places around midnight and move them to secure areas. According to sources, a proposal was subsequently made to restrict nightlife from behind Freedom Square to Konnad beach.

Residents of the Kuttichira area, a heritage site, had earlier expressed their concerns related to the activities of anti-social elements. Thekkeppuram Jagratha Samithi, a collective of residents there, have submitted a memorandum to the District Collector and the District Police Chief seeking restrictions on the Kozhikode beach and Kuttichira between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. K. Moideen Koya, former councillor, and chairperson of the samithi, told The Hindu on Tuesday (November 24) that under Section 440 of the Municipalities Act, the local body’s secretary can issue direct orders to “stop any activity” or “remove any condition that disturbs residents’ rest, sleep, health, or safety”. “The police have promised to strengthen night patrolling in our area. We are planning to install CCTV cameras as well,” he said.

The Kozhikode Corporation, meanwhile, is reportedly toying with the idea of partial restrictions as its cleaning activities at night are getting affected because of the presence of people on the beach.

articles.title: Jagan calls for fair elections in Srikakulam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy spoke to District Collector, Superintendent of Police and other officials, asking them to ensure free and fair elections in the Srikakulam Municipal Corporation, where polling is scheduled to be held on November 26, 2026, said former minister Dharmana Prasada Rao.

Addressing the party’s final public meeting on Tuesday evening, Mr. Prasada said that Mr. Jagan was confident of the victory of YSRCP Mayor candidate Gunda Lakshmi Devi and the corporators in 60 divisions, provided officials discharge their duties impartially, and prevent malpractices and violence.

“YSRCP leaders and activists are ready to face any eventuality on the day of the elections given the large scale violence witnessed during nominations, scrutiny, polling and counting in urban and rural local body elections. The elections in Srikakulam which are being held after a long delay, needs to be conducted in accordance to the rules and regulations. Otherwise, if the YSRCP comes to power in the 2029 Assembly elections, it will take stern action against the officials,” said Mr. Prasada.
Senior party leaders Dharmana Krishnadas, Mandavilli Ravi, Konark Srinivas and others attended the public meeting held in Srikakulam.

articles.title: Guru Nanak’s message of equality, harmony resonates at Prakash Purab
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Thousands of Sikh devotees and people from other faiths gathered at Nampally Exhibition Grounds on Tuesday to celebrate the 557th Prakash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, the founder of Sikhism, with prayers, devotional music and a community meal.

The congregation, held on the occasion of Guru Nanak’s birth anniversary, was jointly organised by the managing committees of Gurudwara Sri Guru Singh Sabha, Ashok Bazar, and Gurudwara Saheb, Secunderabad. The programme began at 11 am and continued until 4.30 pm.
Devotees offered prayers before the Sri Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture of Sikhism, followed by Gurbani kirtan and katha (religious discourse).

Ragi jathas (groups of devotional singers) from different parts of the country performed shabads, including Bhai Maninder Singh of Sri Darbar Sahib, Amritsar, and Bhai Kamaldeep Singh and Bhai Jagteshwar Singh of Patiala. Their renditions highlighted spiritual values and the importance of communal harmony.

Addressing the congregation, preachers recalled Guru Nanak’s teachings of belief in one God, equality irrespective of caste, creed or gender, honest living and selfless service. They said his message continue to hold relevance in a world often divided by social and religious differences.

The celebrations concluded with Guru Ka Langar, the community kitchen tradition in which devotees, irrespective of faith or social background, sat together in rows and shared a meal, reflecting Guru Nanak’s principle of equality and service.

articles.title: Centre to strengthen border surveillance, expand de-addiction centres from 300 to 2,000: Kishan Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Centre has drawn up an ambitious plan to tackle drug abuse by increasing the number of de-addiction centres across the country from 300 to 2,000, strengthening border surveillance, expanding de-addiction facilities and launching a massive awareness campaign aimed at the country’s youth, said Union Minister for Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

He said at a press conference in Hyderabad that special anti-drug units are being established within paramilitary forces, intelligence networks are being strengthened, and the use of sniffer dogs is being enhanced to curb drug trafficking.

An awareness programmes targetting 50 crore youth is being launched and one lakh ‘ Nasha Mukt Bharat Mitra ’ volunteers will be trained in the first phase. The Centre is working towards a drug-free India by 2029 through a “whole-of-government, whole-of-India and whole-of-society” approach under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, said the Minister.
Union Minister of Coal and Mines G. Kishan Reddy addressing a press conference in Hyderabad on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: SIDDHANT THAKUR

Stressing that the fight against drugs cannot be left to law enforcement agencies alone, he called for active participation from parents, teachers, media organisations and citizens. Mr. Kishan Reddy expressed concern over the growing impact of drugs on young people, warning that India’s future would be jeopardised if its youth were not protected from substance abuse.

Referring to Punjab, he said a state once known for its achievements in agriculture and industry had suffered severely because of the drug menace, and cautioned against the spread of similar problems to other parts of the country.

He alleged that drug trafficking networks backed by anti-India elements in neighbouring countries were using narcotics as a means to generate funds for unlawful activities. He also pointed to changing social conditions, including the decline of joint family systems, increasing isolation among youngsters and excessive dependence on mobile phones and social media, as factors contributing to vulnerability to drugs.

Emphasising a compassionate approach, the minister said young drug users should be treated as victims requiring support and rehabilitation rather than as criminals. He urged families, teachers and peers to help affected youth recover with dignity and rejoin mainstream society through continued education and employment opportunities.

Mr. Kishan Reddy also appealed to the Telangana government to preserve public lands for sports facilities and playgrounds, saying initiatives such as K helo India, F it India and yoga could help steer youngsters away from addiction.

articles.title: Kaliningrad: Why Russia’s Baltic exclave is a new flashpoint
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Moscow has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around the strategic exclave and has sent a formal diplomatic note to the NATO over what it sees as attempts to isolate the territory; however, NATO has rejected the accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’

On October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin issued a warning to the West. In a grand hall in Moscow, Mr. Putin sat before an audience of foreign policy experts at the Valdai Discussion Club. “If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation... then, of course, the question of the Russian Federation deploying all types of weapons at our country’s disposal will inevitably and immediately be on the agenda. This is inevitable.”

Mr. Putin continued to insist that Moscow had no plans to attack anyone — neither in 2029, not in 2030, not even in 2050. But if aggression came, he said, Russia would be compelled to respond. European citizens, he added, should understand this clearly. The warning did not appear out of nowhere. For months, NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) countries have been increasing military activities in the Baltic Sea and around Russia’s western borders.

Russia has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around Kaliningrad and has sent a formal diplomatic note to NATO over what Moscow sees as attempts to isolate the territory. NATO, however, has rejected those accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’.

“I can confirm that Russia sent a non-paper to NATO and that we have sent a response, noting that NATO is a defensive alliance and none of our activities or exercises pose a risk to any part of Russia,” said alliance spokesperson Allison Hart. “We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric,” she added.

articles.title: Estonia on the edge as Russia-NATO tensions rise
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The NATO member is overhauling its military strategy, moving troops closer to the border and investing in long-range arms as Russia is carrying out grey-zone tactics in NATO’s eastern flank; the country’s defence spending is set to rise by 42% in 2026, reaching €2.4 billion, or around 5.4% of its GDP; the U.K. has maintained some 1,200 troops in Estonia as part of NATO’s forward defence

On October 12, NATO’s top military commander issued a stark warning to Russia. General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, said that if Moscow were “foolish enough” to attack an alliance territory, NATO would destroy “anything and everything” involved in the attack.
His remarks came at a time of rising tensions between Russia and European nations. And one country that finds itself under pressure on the hot Russia-NATO border is the tiny Estonia.

When the U.S., Canada, and 10 other European nations came together in 1949, in the early phase of the Cold War, to form the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), they had a clear goal. As Lord Hastings Lionel Ismay, the alliance’s first Secretary General, famously put it, the purpose was to “keep the Soviet Union out, the Americans in, and the Germans down.”

Throughout the Cold War, NATO had been the primary military bulwark against Soviet power in Europe. After the disintegration of the Soviet Union in 1991, Russia fell into a phase of strategic retreat, while NATO expanded towards Eastern Europe. This set the stage for renewed tensions once Russia started reasserting itself in the region.
The situation became even more complicated after Russia annexed Crimea in 2014 and launched its invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

articles.title: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government

Three weeks after President Lula da Silva’s election victory, Brazilian institutions are tightening the screws on Big Tech over alleged interference in favour of his far-right rival Flávio Bolsonaro during the campaign. The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference from outside through digital platforms. We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula told his supporters after winning the election on October 25.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the Brazilian government stepped up efforts to pass a bill which would give the country’s competition regulator (CADE) more powers to monitor the Big Tech operations. Pending since September 2025, the bill is modelled on European Union regulations and it faces opposition from Bolsonaro allies.

Meanwhile, both Big Tech and the Bolsonaro camp are feeling the heat. In a landmark ruling on November 10, Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) fined Meta 7.5 million reais (US$1.5 million) for “failing to provide complete information” in a case alleging bias in the distribution of online content. The decision came after a civil society group filed a petition accusing Meta of restricting pro-Lula posts while allowing content favouring Flávio during the campaign. Meta has dismissed the allegations as “false and unfounded”, but internal documents of the company, exposed by Brazilian media, showed that Lula’s Instagram accounts had been restricted during the campaign.

In another decision that can have far-reaching consequences for Flavio and his Liberal Party (PL), a Brazilian Supreme Court judge has ordered the Federal Police (PF) to investigate possible foreign interference in the electoral process, with focus on hidden financing of campaigns. In his order, Justice Flávio Dino cited allegations that two Brazilian businessmen acted on behalf of the US-based Rockbridge Network to raise funds for Flávio’s campaign in the United States. “The prohibition on foreign financing under Brazilian law has a parallel in the US as well. For this reason, it is even more important that resources allegedly originating from that country should not be allowed to influence the Brazilian election,” the judge said in his order.

The Rockbridge Network is an American right-wing organisation co-founded in 2019 by US Vice-President JD Vance and businessman Chris Buskirk, with tech billionaire Peter Thiel bringing them together. Justice Dino has directed the police to investigate whether money and services were channelled to Flávio’s campaign. He also cited concerns over Meta’s handling of political content, including an October 22 report by the company’s Oversight Board highlighting gaps in safeguards for electoral integrity and concerns raised by United Nations observers on October 21.

articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

With a smirk, Flávio Bolsonaro squinted at the camera and called President Lula da Silva “nine fingers” in the televised debate just two days before Brazil went to the polls for the presidential runoff. It was a cynical attempt to weaponise an old scar – and a gossip – against the Workers Party’s leader. Lula reacted sharply, reminding the audience how he had lost a finger on his left hand while working in a factory. “If there is anyone who lost a finger at the age of 17, it was me, working at night because I had to work,” Lula said, staring into the cameras. A red-faced Flavio didn’t know where to look. On October 25, Lula made history by becoming the first Brazilian president to finish second in the first round of an election, held on October 4, and go on to win the presidency in the run-off.

Ever since Lula entered politics more than three decades ago, his opponents have peddled the rumour that he deliberately chopped off his own finger to gain sympathy and claim compensation. But those familiar with his life know the struggles that shaped him. Born on October 27, 1945, in a dusty corner of Brazil, Lula grew up amid hunger and deprivation in the state of Pernambuco.

His family migrated to São Paulo in search of a better life, joining thousands who fled the region trapped in poverty and hopelessness. Raised by his mother, Dona Lindu, whose resilience left a lasting impression on him, Lula received only primary education before joining the workforce as a teenager. His mother passed away at 64 in 1980, while Lula was in prison during a workers’ strike. “I believe in a more just country because one day my mother taught me that, even in a simple home, no one can give up,” Lula said on Mother’s Day this year, fighting back tears as he remembered Dona Lindu.

Lula’s journey – from a parched corner of Brazil to the industrial belt of Sao Paulo – was brought to life in Lula, the Son of Brazil , a 2010 film directed by Fábio Barreto. Tracking his life, the film showed how Lula’s political training began on the factory floors of Sao Paulo’s industrial region known for its massive factories.

Amid the clutter of machines and the daily struggle with poverty, Lula rose from an apprentice to a metalworker and trade union leader and became the voice of workers who were not willing to accept low wages and political exclusion. “During the late 1970s, as Brazil’s military dictatorship sought to contain dissent, Lula emerged as one of the most prominent figures in the labour movement. His leadership brought him into direct confrontation with the regime and in 1980 he was arrested for his role in the strikes,” said Mr. Barreto.

articles.title: Indian space companies sign largest-of-its-kind deal on satellite systems
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Bellatrix Aerospace to supply in-space propulsion systems for GalaxEye’s 30 satellites

Indian space companies GalaxEye and Bellatrix Aerospace on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) signed a multi-year contract in which Bellatrix Aerospace will supply in-space propulsion systems for the next 30 satellites GalaxEye is building.

This made the deal the “largest business-to-business order” one Indian private space company has placed with another since the space sector opened to private players in 2020, a press release noted. While private companies have participated in India’s space sector since inception, it has usually been as suppliers to the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).
The GalaxEye-Bellatrix deal was unveiled at the 5th India International Space Conclave, organised by the Indian Space Association (ISpA). The financial details of the contract were not disclosed.

GalaxEye is building the world’s first OptoSAR satellite constellation. OptoSAR is a proprietary imaging technology that allows customers to see any place on Earth through clouds, smoke, and darkness. Bellatrix builds the thrusters that steer and position satellites once they reach orbit, with hardware already flight-tested on ISRO missions.

“OptoSAR satellites are demanding customers. They need precise, repeatable orbits across a whole constellation, not a single demonstration. Our thrusters have already fired in orbit on ISRO missions, and we have built the production lines to deliver that same performance at constellation scale,” Rohan M. Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of Bellatrix Aerospace, said in a statement. Bellatrix makes electric and green propulsion systems for satellites and orbital transfer vehicles.

Mission Drishti, launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 on May 3, 2026, became the world’s first OptoSAR satellite in orbit. It validated GalaxEye’s spacecraft deployment, attitude control, onboard computing and in-house mission operations before contact was lost after a geomagnetic storm, the company stated.

In September, the Department of Science and Technology’s Technology Development Board committed ₹63.84 crore from the Government of India’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund for GalaxEye’s next multi-sensor satellite, which targets imagery sharper than 0.5 metres. Sourcing propulsion from a partner in the same city gives GalaxEye closer engineering control and shorter lead times as it builds that satellite.
“Drishti taught us that every critical system on a satellite has to be one we can see, test and improve up close,” Suyash Singh, co-founder and CEO of GalaxEye, said in a statement.

ISRO chairman V. Narayanan said that private industry was now indispensable to India’s space ecosystem. “Today, we are extremely happy that 440 start-up companies are working in the space area. Whenever a launch vehicle lifts off or we place a satellite, 70-80% of the budget is pumped into the Indian industry. Without the support of Indian industry, we would not have reached the present level.”

Other officials, however, pointed out while India was putting in place a system to increase capacity, it had to work towards increasing demand for products from the private space ecosystem. “The first phase of India’s space reforms opened the sector and created an institutional framework for private participation. Now India has to work on generating heavy demand. I have less concern about capacity being created; I see a bigger need for demand to be created. The second is to have enough money coming into the sector, and number three, to have procedures at all levels. Space is not a sector that is going to give you a payback in six months or nine months. Perseverance is required, and the government must continue to have policy stability,” said Pawan Goenka, chairman, InSpace, India’s single-window regulatory and promotional body for the private space sector.

But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Even a low base effect could not push India’s oil and gas sectors into growth

The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Incomplete remedies: On Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The ECI offers relief to a section of deleted electors but SIR’s flaws remain

Following the Special Summary Revision (SSR) by the Election Commission of India (ECI) in some States that had undergone the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) , mostly in Phases 1 and 2, some 74 lakh names were added onto the electoral rolls. This meant that the electorate in those 13 States, that had shrunk from 49.61 crore to 45.22 crore after the SIR, has now gone up to 45.96 crore. The ECI has extended the SSR to States and UTs in Phase 3. As before, it requires no proof of citizenship or mapping to older rolls, and insists on personal notice before any deletion other than of the dead. It also directs Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) to cross-verify deletions personally wherever they exceed 2% of a polling station’s electors. Draft deletions in Phase 3 of the SIR averaged 17% , and reached 32.8% in Delhi . The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. The ECI’s use of remedies that existed in the registration rules is a tacit admission that it went wrong during the SIR. But the measures are limited. They reach roughly 4.5 crore of the 13.37 crore struck off the draft rolls and do not cover electors who moved out of their States. Electors in States where the SIR has concluded, including Bihar and West Bengal, which have already voted on the SIR rolls, can return only through the SSR, by filing Form 6 as new voters, with fresh EPIC numbers and no record that they were ever on the roll. In essence, the structure of the SIR remains intact. Electors must still provide details from “the last SIR”, and those whose details are unavailable or do not match will be asked for documents in a manner that amounts to a citizenship test. The legality of the ludicrous “logical discrepancy” checks remains unaddressed. The 2002-03 special revision offered a better way. Those who had shifted homes were enumerated door to door at their new addresses. The Supreme Court must direct the ECI to return to that model.

The ECI also offered another opportunity to electors deleted by the SIR in the seven States and UTs where it is still underway, such as Delhi and Maharashtra, to return to the rolls. Electors who did not return their forms can do so now, explaining the delay, and those who moved within the State can return through the enumeration form with proof of their new address. EROs will process these forms under Rule 21(1) of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and restore the elector’s old EPIC number.

These “corrective” measures follow the Supreme Court’s observation on October 28 that forcing deleted electors to re-enrol through Form 6, meant for new voters, was an “error”. articles.title: Talks without peace: On Russia, Ukraine, U.S. talks
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Europe must be part of any settlement on the Ukraine war

The trilateral negotiations in Abu Dhabi between Russia, Ukraine and the U.S. earlier this month failed to produce a major breakthrough or bridge the wide gap between Kyiv and Moscow. Yet, they were a good beginning towards finding a political settlement to Europe’s longest war since the Second World War . In the two-day talks, hosted by the U.S., the warring sides agreed on some humanitarian measures, including prisoner exchange. U.S. representatives Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow after the talks to discuss the proposal. In the next stage, U.S., Ukrainian and European officials will meet in Berlin to discuss a coordinated European and Ukrainian position towards the peace process. As of now, Russian and Ukrainian positions remain far apart. Russia demands Ukraine withdraw from the territories of Donbas it still controls to stop attacks. Russia also wants to introduce limits to Ukrainian military capabilities and Kyiv to declare neutrality (give up its NATO ambitions). Ukraine, on the other hand, has rejected making any territorial concessions for a settlement and asked for security guarantees from the West so that Russia would not attack the country again.

That Ukraine survived Russia’s invasion and continued to resist Russian forces for almost five years is no small feat. But it has also paid a huge price for its resistance. The country has lost more than 20% of its territory. Millions have fled, while men of fighting age are being drafted into the military . Ukraine’s economy is kept afloat by European support, while its military continues to rely on NATO for weapons and other supplies. Until recently, the West stood united in its support for Ukraine against Russia, but that unity has since begun to fray. U.S. President Donald Trump, who has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel, is seeking to reset Washington’s ties with Moscow . European leaders, who initially sought to isolate Russia, have also started reestablishing contacts with the Kremlin. In October, Finnish and Norwegian leaders held direct talks with Mr. Putin. To be sure, Ukraine’s long-range strikes can hurt Russia, as the recent attack on the Kerch Bridge demonstrated. But such strikes are unlikely to change the Kremlin’s thinking about the war. As the conflict drags on, Ukraine’s position is weakening, and its allies are growing increasingly divided. After almost five years, Russia has failed to take a decisive victory. Ukraine does not have a credible path towards victory either. A diplomatic settlement, therefore, is the only way forward. The Abu Dhabi talks recognised this reality. But for the process to be meaningful, Europe must also be brought to the negotiating table.

articles.title: Kasimedu fisherfolk withdraw strike after Minister’s intervention
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fishermen of Kasimedu on Sunday withdrew their indefinite strike, seeking the release of eight boats impounded by the Andhra Pradesh government, after the intervention of Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, who is also the MLA for Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar Assembly constituency.
The Minister, who reached the fishing harbour on Sunday morning, interacted with the leaders of various associations, and listened to their grievances for about an hour.
The fisherfolk had also demanded that the State government increase the solatium paid to the kin of fishermen who died in Cyclone Murasu.
Mr. Marie Wilson said he had taken up their issues with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, and that steps would be taken to increase the compensation and bring the boats back.

A former Fisheries Department official said the boats had been impounded in Andhra Pradesh since April, without the relevant provisions of the Marine Fisheries Regulation Act being implemented. “Under the Act, the Nellore Collector, should have issued notice to the boat owners, summoned them and made them pay the requisite fine. However, this has not been done.”
Also, no action has been taken by the Andhra Pradesh government on the boats from Karaikal that had fished close to their coast.
“The fishermen from Karaikal were the ones who had escaped along with their boats that were impounded in Andhra Pradesh,” said another source.

articles.title: Over 4,850 buses, 16 special trains to run for Karthigai Deepam in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments S. Ramesh inspects civic and security arrangements made for devotees ahead of the festival
Sixteen special trains and 4,877 buses will be operated to Tiruvannamalai town from November 23-25 as part of Karthigai Deepam festival.

On Sunday, Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) S. Ramesh inspected civic and security arrangements made for devotees ahead of the festival, including Maha Deepam (November 24). District Collector Vandhana Garg was also present.

“More than 15,500 police personnel will be deployed in the town for security purposes. Around 1,100 CCTV cameras including 556 surveillance box cameras have also been roped as part of safety measures,” Mr. Ramesh said.

The district administration has set up 26 temporary bus termini, mostly on the outskirts of the town, with 26 diesel-run generators. The transport department will operate 160 free shuttle services between the temporary bus termini and various parts of the town, including the 14-km Girivalam path and Arunachaleswarar Temple. As per estimates, around 50 lakh devotees are expected for the festival.

As part of annadanam (distribution of free food), 288 spots were allotted for volunteers to distribute free food to visitors. Seven food safety testing teams will monitor the quality of the food distributed in these spots.
All private vehicles, including tourist cabs, are prohibited from entering the town to provide more road space for walkers to reach the temple. It will help to prevent congestion and stampedes.

Vehicles can be parked at any of the 155 parking lots that are away from the town, where over 21,000 vehicles can be parked. Jute mats will be laid for at least a distance of two km on the footpaths to allow visitors to walk to the temple safely. Children at the festival will be given wristbands to ensure their safety.

The health department has set up 120 medical camps, mostly on the Girivalam path and bus terminuses, for the festival. Around 35 ambulances including 10 bike ambulances, have also been roped. Adequate water taps (146 spots), washrooms (600 spots), and 10,900 streetlights have been set up for the festival. A total of 2,466 sanitation staff were roped in to keep the town clean of trash.

To ensure the safety of visitors, 31 police watch towers that will be supported by 350 bike patrols and 62 help desks in the town round the clock. Around 110 firefighters with 26 water tenders will be deployed to prevent accidental fires, especially on the hillock during Maha Deepam. For emergencies during the festival, helpline numbers are: 04175-233344; 04175-233345; 8072797683.

Inspector Manjith Lal was suspended by District Police Chief (Kochi City) R. Nishanthini pending an inquiry, based on an internal report which found prima facie irregularities and a serious violation of discipline, as per the suspension order.

articles.title: Congress leaders from Keralam urge AICC to restore consultations within party ahead of UDF’s policy decisions
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: K.C. Joseph, Benny Behanan, Shafi Parambil meet Mallikarjun Kharge, air grievances about a 'dormant' party apparatus stemming from the lack of a full-time State president and delayed reorganisation. Their demands include a hands-on party president

Top Congress leaders from arguably “rival factions” are seeking the All India Congress Committee (AICC)’s intervention to address what they see as a lack of consultation, which they contend makes consensus elusive when the United Democratic Front (UDF) government decides policy and pushes key political appointments.

Veteran Congress leader K.C. Joseph; Benny Behanan, MP; and Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) working president Shafi Parambil are the latest among the top Keralam leaders to go to New Delhi to ostensibly air their grievances about a “dormant” party apparatus stemming, chiefly, from the lack of a full-time State president and “delayed” reorganisation.

Notably, Mr. Behanan is also among the top four contenders for the KPCC president post, with the incumbent and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph demanding that he be relieved of the job so he can focus solely on his Cabinet responsibilities. Others in the race include Congress Working Committee (CWC) president Kodikunnil Suresh, Joseph Vazhakkan, and Ajay Tharayil.

Mr. K.C. Joseph told The Hindu that the trio had met AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge. “The KPCC office is largely deserted these days. The desolation telegraphs an atrophied, almost moribund party machinery to the rank-and-file. A hands-on party president and swift reorganisation from the top down is the only panacea to the torpor that has beset the Congress in Kerala,” he said. Mr. Joseph said the meeting was “anything but about censuring any person or apportioning blame”. He said the party and the government have to march in lockstep.

“We have demanded the constitution of a party committee to look into impending appointments to boards and corporations earmarked for Congress workers. The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) has a similar structure,” Mr. Joseph said.

Another Congress insider said the demand for organisational restructuring and institution of a consultative mechanism to weigh policy and key nominations was gaining ground in the party in Kerala. He said many leaders feared that the delay in rectifying the current “organisational lacunae” could feed factionalism.

Months earlier, United Democratic Front (UDF) convener Adoor Prakash, MP, had met Mr. Kharge and complained about the lack of consultation in the ruling alliance, which he said had rendered the apex political structure redundant.

Mr. Joseph’s visit also came as the Left Democratic Front (LDF) accused Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan of bypassing the Cabinet and the UDF, leaving key decision-making to a “power group” centred on the Cabinet. Notably, Mr. Joseph, Mr. Behanan and Mr. Parambil, widely regarded as leaders of the so-called “A-group” in the KPCC, had met Mr. Satheesan earlier and raised the same demands.

articles.title: Most of the 12.22 lakh electors removed during SIR yet to apply for inclusion in the rolls
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Only 83,972 voters have been included in the electoral rolls after the SIR. Many residents of rental accommodation say they need assistance for inclusion. Officials point to lack of awareness among the residents of the SIR

Most of the 12.22 lakh electors, whose names were removed during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Chennai district after they were classified as “permanently shifted”, are yet to apply for inclusion of their names in the electoral rolls.

According to estimates, 51% of the residents in Chennai own a house, while 49% live in rental accommodation. Many electors who shifted their residence before the 2026 Assembly election complained that they did not vote this year as their names were removed from the rolls. However, only 83,972 voters in the city have been included in the rolls after the SIR. Many residents of rental accommodation have said they need assistance for including their names in the rolls.

B. Raja, who is living in rental accommodation, was an elector under a polling booth at Chintadripet in the Chepauk-Thiruvallikeni Assembly Constituency until the 2024 Lok Sabha election. This Assembly election, he visited the polling booth, but was not permitted to vote because his name was removed during the SIR after he shifted to another house in the city.

“Many residents like me who have to shift to new rental houses frequently could not vote in the Assembly election at our booth because we did not know what to do. We may need assistance. Once we start visiting a government office, we have to spend a lot of time,” he said.

Officials point to lack of awareness among the residents of the SIR. Not many residents who lost their votes visited the camps conducted by the Chennai District Election Office on Sunday (November 22, 2026) for inclusion of their names in the rolls.

Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said, “Wide publicity has been given to the camps [held on Sunday]. Furthermore, this process is continuous. Online applications can also be used. We will again cross-check the absent, shifted voters, as emerged during the SIR, and ensure that no eligible voters are left out of the rolls... Electoral camps in colleges will be part of this drive.”

“After the SIR, multiple rounds of opportunities have been given to eligible voters to become part of the rolls. As many as 83,972 voters have been included in the rolls since the final electoral rolls came out after the SIR, and the draft roll was published for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) on November 12. We will hold special camps again on November 29. Enough publicity has been given to that too,” Dr. Sameeran said.

“Another way to publicise it is through Booth Level Agents (BLAs). We have created awareness at our meetings with political parties. We have not received any major claim and objection or complaint from members of the public about denial of opportunity to register their names. Nevertheless, we will intensify voter registration during this SSR. Residents have been requested to lodge complaints with the District Election Office with details so that we can find solutions,” Dr. Sameeran said.

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector.
The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids.
Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said.
The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

“Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement.

Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

articles.title: Pattabiram residents urge Highways dept. to build roundabouton CTH Road junction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Residents of Pattabiram have urged the Highways Department to build a roundabout on the Chennai–Tiruvallur High Road (CTH) or Chennai–Tirupati–Renigunta Road near the flyover, replacing the Level Crossing 2 on the railway siding.
Without a roundabout, the six-way junction presents a chaotic sight during peak hours, said Roy Rozario, a resident.
Apart from the lanes of the C.T.H Road, road to/from Poonamallee and M.G. Road join the junction. People heading to the police station, TIDEL Park, hotels, schools, and colleges use the junction.

“Due to the lack of a roundabout, a lot of accidents happen as people drive on the wrong side of the road or drive recklessly. Long ago, the government had announced that a roundabout would be constructedat the location. We hope that it would come up soon,” he added.

Residents, meanwhile, have urged the department to open the other side of the flyover to traffic. “It has been completed. Only some works such as lighting, removal of excess cement concrete, and painting seem to remain. Though the surface is rough, people are driving on the incomplete side of the flyover to reach the other side,” said T. Sadagopan, activist.
The space beneath the flyover must also be cleared and the roads must be laid properly.

“Several bus services from Poonamallee, Thiruninravur, and other places have been cut, as there is no space to park the buses. Those buses that start from Pattabiram wait at random spots on the C.T.H Road. We want the Highways to also construct a foot overbridge beneath the flyover, or a limited-use subway,” said a resident.
Sources said the roundabout would be formed during the widening of the road. As far as a subway or a foot overbridge was concerned, necessary studies would be taken up.

articles.title: Six sent to juvenile home after Mumbai assault; Maharashtra SP leader seeks age change
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Police registered a case and produced all eight before the Board, and notices were sent to parents; the case was registered under sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352 and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, says Deputy Commissioner of Police

A juvenile court in Mumbai on Saturday sent six minors to a juvenile correctional home till December 4 in connection with the alleged assault of a couple at a garden in Kurla on Friday evening, police said on Sunday. The six are aged between 12 and 15, the Ghatkopar police said.

Deputy Commissioner of Police Ganesh Shinde said an FIR was lodged against the minors under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 118(1) (voluntarily causing hurt using dangerous weapons or means), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), and 351(2) (criminal intimidation) and other relevant provisions of the BNS.
All of them were produced before the Juvenile Justice Board and notices were sent to their parents.

According to the police, the couple was at the garden behind Phoenix Marketcity mall when a group of minors surrounded them and began to abuse them. When the couple tried to reason with the group, they assaulted them with a hockey stick and forced them out of the garden. Police detained them after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.
The police said they are recording the statements of the couple and the juveniles to determine whether the two groups had a dispute before the incident that took place at the Pramod Mahajan Garden.

The incident drew sharp reactions from political parties, with many condemning it. Samajwadi Party Maharashtra president Abu Asim Azmi said the juvenile age threshold should be brought down from 18 to 15 and that those below 18 years who commit murder, robbery or harassment should not be given concessions under the law. Mr. Azmi added that the incident should not be linked to religion and that the law should act without discrimination.
Meanwhile, BJP leader Kirit Somaiya met the couple at the Ghatkopar police station and promised action.

NCP (SP) MP Supriya Sule urged Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, who holds the Home portfolio, to “adopt a no-tolerance policy towards such incidents” and said citizens should be able to move around freely in the State.
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui also condemned the assault.

articles.title: Over 40% Group A posts vacant at PGIMS Rohtak, says former Minister
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Alleging that 41.6% of the sanctioned Group A posts at the Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGIMS) in Rohtak were lying vacant, former Haryana Home Minister Subhash Batra on Sunday questioned the BJP government’s claims of improving healthcare services in the State.

Citing an inspection by the Assembly’s Subject Committee in February, Mr. Batra said 424 of the 1,018 sanctioned Group A posts at the institute were vacant. He said the shortage of doctors, specialists and healthcare staff was affecting patient care at the institute, which catered to over 8,000 patients daily in its outpatient department.
Manjunath, in-charge of the Public Relations Department, PGIMS, did not respond to repeated calls and messages seeking his response to the former Minister’s allegations.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Batra also pointed out that only 200 of the 540 medicines on the government-approved list were available in the hospital store during the Health Minister’s inspection in April. Supply orders for 172 types of medicines and surgical materials were pending with companies, he alleged.

Alleging that the “condition of the Radiology Department is also extremely concerning”, Mr. Batra said 10 of the 13 sanctioned faculty posts and nine of the 11 Senior Resident posts were vacant in the department, as per a September-October 2026 report. Of the nearly 500 patients advised ultrasound examinations daily, only 40% could undergo the test on the same day, he added.

Questioning the gap between budgetary allocations and the availability of health care facilities, Mr. Batra said ₹1,232 crore had been allocated to the Pandit Bhagwat Dayal Sharma University of Health Sciences and PGIMS for 2026-27, an increase of ₹422 crore over the previous year, but patients continued to face shortages of medicines and delays in diagnostic tests.
Mr. Batra also raised concerns over two incidents of ceiling plaster falling in the old hospital building in October.

On behalf of the Congress, Mr. Batra demanded that all vacant posts be filled, medicine stocks and pending complaints be made public, diagnostic facilities expanded and old hospital buildings subjected to a safety audit.

“The poor, labourers, farmers and the middle-class families in the State need doctors on time, essential medicines and quality treatment and not speeches and announcements,” he said, adding that the Congress would continue to raise this serious issue concerning health and hold the government accountable.

articles.title: 18th U.P. Legislative Assembly sits less than 90 days, experts point to unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose the chance to raise people-centric issues making legislature a passive spectator; experts call it contrary to spirit of constitutional checks and balance

With hardly two months left for Uttar Pradesh assembly polls and the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (May 2022- March 2027) nearing completion, question marks have been raised over the fewer days/meetings of the Legislative Assembly in the last five years.
Editorial | Stoop to conquer: On the Opposition’s seat-sharing ahead of U.P. polls

As the 18th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly functioned for only 84 days, an average of 17 days a year, Opposition parties and constitutional experts in the State said fewer functioning days directly limit legislative oversight, and MLAs lose opportunities to raise constituency-centric issues.
They added that in a State having a population of over 25 crores (250 million people), at least 50 days of Assembly sessions per year, similar to the Lok Sabha, are necessary.

As per the data accessed by The Hindu and reverified through the data available with PRS Legislative Research as well as the U.P. Legislative Assembly Official Website, the State Assembly functioned for 16 days in 2022, 20 days in 2023, 16 days in 2024, 18 days in 2025 and 14 days in 2026 till now. The Assembly functioned for only over 500 hours in the last roughly five years in 15 sessions. In comparison, the 17 th Lok Sabha, which functioned between June 2019 and May 2024, functioned for 274 days, across 15 sessions, averaging 55 sitting/days per year.

“The nearing conclusion of the tenure of the 18 th Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly presents an unsettling indictment of legislative governance in India’s most populous State. A House entrusted with representing more than 25 crore citizens reportedly sat for only 84 days over its five-year tenure, averaging just 17 sitting days a year. Such infrequent sittings are not a matter of administrative convenience; they strike at the heart of the constitutional scheme of accountable government. For a State grappling with enormous developmental challenges, law-and-order concerns and a population larger than that of most countries, such limited legislative engagement is indefensible. If the Lok Sabha can meet for around sixty days annually, Uttar Pradesh should institutionalize at least fifty sitting days every year as a constitutional minimum. Democracy is not sustained merely by periodic elections; it survives through continuous legislative vigilance. A Legislature that seldom meets risks converting representative government into a constitutional ritual and reducing executive accountability to an illusion. Such a trend ought to alarm every citizen who values constitutionalism, democratic oversight and the rule of law,” said Syed Mohammad Haider Rizvi, an expert on Constitutional Law and Legislative Processes and practicing advocate based in Lucknow.

Sudhir Panwar, a senior Samajwadi Party (SP) leader said, “the Constitution distributed power and responsibility between legislature and executive for efficient working of democratic system. The legislature is responsible for oversight on functioning of executive and budget scrutiny. There is a fine balance between executive and legislative; fewer sitting disturb that balance in favor of the executive. The other dimension is relationship between fewer sitting and concentration of power in political system and those at helm of affairs as Chief Minister. In state assembly for continuous working, the committee system like Parliament needs to be introduced,”.

Highlighting the Constitutional provisions, Mr. Rizvi added that when the Assembly sits for barely a handful of days each year, legislative oversight becomes diluted, financial scrutiny under Articles 202 to 207 becomes truncated, and the representatives of the people are deprived of sufficient opportunities to raise constituency-centric concerns, and the inevitable consequence is an unhealthy concentration of power in the Executive, contrary to the spirit of constitutional checks and balances.

“The Constitution of India envisages a Legislature that is not a passive spectator but an active constitutional check upon executive authority. Articles 163 and 164 make the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly, a responsibility that can be meaningfully enforced only when the House meets frequently enough to question, debate, scrutinize, and hold the Government to account. Likewise, Article 174 requires the Legislature to meet at regular intervals and clearly contemplates a living, functioning institution rather than one that assembles merely to satisfy the minimum constitutional formality. In constitutional theory and democratic practice alike, the Legislature is the foremost forum through which the sovereign will of the people finds expression,” he said.
Uttar Pradesh / executive (government) / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: ‘The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded; the two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,’ the two parties said in a joint statement

The parties of caretaker Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday (November 22, 2026) without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday (November 22).

"The latest round of coalition talks... has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail," the two parties said in a joint statement.
"A follow-up meeting will be held," they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, with the possibility of a 14?day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.

His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra?Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men, a mechanism already tried in Israel.

Such an arrangement could allow Netanyahu to keep his political protection against the corruption charges he faces, as well as continue to oppose the creation of an independent commission of inquiry into the security failures that preceded the Hamas attack of October 7, 2023.
But that prospect runs up against Eisenkot's refusal to serve in a cabinet led by Netanyahu, against whom he centred his campaign.
His ally Naftali Bennett, a former prime minister, also reiterated on Saturday his refusal to join a coalition with "Netanyahu or his bloc, under any circumstances".

On Saturday (November 22), Yashar presented the resumption of talks as "a genuine commitment to forming the broadest possible government", saying that Eisenkot had asked his representatives to explore all options.
But Likud immediately laid down several conditions for its participation in a unity government, a formula backed by Mr. Netanyahu.
