articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

Amandeep Garg, who was leading India’s delegation but speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson on behalf of the LMDC, said on the floor: “Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, we are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.” The LMDC expressed “concern” about the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibility not being adequately reflected, adding that there was a “dilution” of the principle of developed countries taking historical responsibility and meeting their obligations.

“At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? The cover decision does not reflect this, and only repeats agreed paragraphs from previous decisions to reflect responsibility and does not connect this with the imminent prospect of exceeding 1.5 deg. C,” he said.

🌐 International Affairs 📅 23 Nov 2026 • IN-APP NEWSPAPER PRINT EDITION

COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics

EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries.

On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.”

“We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU.

“We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added.

A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties.

Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”.

“Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator.

On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against explicit language on fossil fuel and expressed comfort with the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

Amandeep Garg, who was leading India’s delegation but speaking in his capacity as a spokesperson on behalf of the LMDC, said on the floor: “Everyone has worked tirelessly, and despite our discomfort with some elements of the text, we are willing to move forward, and continue to engage.” The LMDC expressed “concern” about the principles of equity and common but differentiated responsibility not being adequately reflected, adding that there was a “dilution” of the principle of developed countries taking historical responsibility and meeting their obligations.

“At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? The cover decision does not reflect this, and only repeats agreed paragraphs from previous decisions to reflect responsibility and does not connect this with the imminent prospect of exceeding 1.5 deg. C,” he said.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “At the threshold of crossing 1.5 deg. C, we have raised a fundamental point – we need to reflect why we are here. Whose emissions, both past and continuing, have exhausted the global carbon budget? The cover decision does not reflect this, and only repeats agreed paragraphs from previous decisions to reflect responsibility and does not connect this with the imminent prospect of exceeding 1.5 deg. C,” he said.

articles.title: Supreme Court says, right to seek correction of electoral roll entry is personal, can't be pursued in PIL
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: A Bench comprising CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it was not inclined to entertain the plea
The Supreme Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) dismissed a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) seeking corrections to municipal electoral rolls in Uttar Pradesh over discrepancies in house numbers.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it was not inclined to entertain the plea.

“The right to seek correction of an electoral-roll entry is personal to the individual voter and cannot ordinarily be pursued collectively through a PIL. The municipal electoral rolls are governed by their own rules, and individual voters can approach the competent election authorities for corrections,” Justice Bagchi orally observed.

The petitioner had argued that house numbers had changed, representations remained unaddressed and municipal electoral rolls should be aligned with those used for parliamentary and Assembly elections.

articles.title: Hyderabad bomb threat email sender used Europe-based VPN, temporary email account
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cybercrime teams are working to trace the sender of the threatening email, which warned of 26/11-style attacks and named Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza as targets

The sender of the bomb threat email, received by Hyderabad Police , reportedly used a Europe-based Virtual Private Network (VPN) and a temporary email account to conceal their identity, making it difficult for investigators to trace the origin of the message.

The cybercrime teams are working to identify the sender by analysing the digital trail left behind by the email, which threatened 26/11-style attacks in the city and named Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza as potential targets.

The email, received on Saturday (November 21, 2026), reportedly claimed that the attacks would be carried out in retaliation for the killing of Lashkar-e-Taiba operative Lateef Bhat in Jammu and Kashmir. It threatened to kill at least 300 people.

The police have intensified security at the locations mentioned in the email and other crowded public places, including railway stations, hotels, bus terminals and religious places. Bomb detection squads and sniffer dog teams conducted anti-sabotage checks, but no explosives were found.

The investigators are examining the email and associated digital information to establish the sender’s identity and verify the authenticity of the threat. The use of a VPN and a temporary email account has complicated the tracing process, with teams working to establish the origin of the message.
The police have appealed to citizens not to panic or circulate unverified information and asked them to report suspicious persons or unattended objects by dialling 112.

articles.title: Adityanath hails Ayodhya-Janakpur rail link as new chapter in India-Nepal cultural ties
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: ‘The centuries-old, unbroken emotional and cultural relationship between India and Nepal will now be further strengthened through modern rail connectivity,’ Yogi Adityanath said

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the start of a direct rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur in Nepal will open a new chapter in the centuries-old spiritual and cultural ties between the two regions and would strengthen India-Nepal relations and facilitate pilgrimage for crores of devotees.

In a post on X ahead of the inauguration, Mr. Adityanath said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balen Shah would jointly flag off the rail service connecting Ayodhya, the holy city associated with Lord Ram, and Janakpur, the birthplace of Goddess Sita.
Keep track | Nepal PM India visit LIVE: Balen Shah begins bilateral visit; energy, connectivity on agenda
"The centuries-old, unbroken emotional and cultural relationship between India and Nepal will now be further strengthened through modern rail connectivity," he said.
Referring to the traditional 'roti-beti' ties between the Awadh and Mithila regions, the chief minister said a new golden chapter was being added to their spiritual, cultural and social relationship.
Mr. Adityanath said he would be present in Ayodhya to witness the occasion, which he described as one that would bring alive memories of the Treta Yuga.
He said the initiative was a reflection of Mr. Modi's vision of 'heritage as well as development' and the 'Neighbourhood First' policy.
"The pilgrimage of crores of devotees from both countries will become easier, while religious tourism, cultural integration and regional prosperity will also receive a new impetus," he said.
Describing the rail service as a gift that would bring Awadh and Mithila closer, Mr. Adityanath extended his heartfelt congratulations to devotees of Lord Ram.

The Saryu-Kamala Express will be operated using modern 17-coach LHB (Linke Hofmann Busch) rakes. The train configuration includes eight air-conditioned coaches, seven sleeper-class coaches, one LSLRD (LHB Second Class, Luggage, Brake, and Disabled-friendly) coach, and one LWLRRM (LHB Power Car/Generator-cum-Luggage-cum-Brake Van) coach.

The express train, to be available for regular service from November 28, will take about 19 hours to cover the 604-kilometre distance between Ayodhya Cantt and Janakpur Dham. Passengers will not need to change trains during the journey.

The service will operate once a week, departing from Ayodhya Cantt every Monday at 5:50 p.m. and reaching Janakpur Dham at 12:40 p.m. (Nepali time) on Tuesday (November 24). It will pass through Mankapur, Basti, Gorakhpur, Narkatiaganj, Raxaul, Sitamarhi, Shisho, Madhubani, and Jaynagar.

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The suspended students were then taken to the SSUS campus in a triumphant march carrying a banner that read, “The people united will never be defeated”

Euphoric and emotional scenes unfolded at the protest pandal outside the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit (SSUS) at Kalady on Monday (November 23, 2026) following the Kerala High Court order setting aside the suspension of 16 students and directing their immediate reinstatement.

The suspended students, owing allegiance to the Students Federation of India (SFI), who had been on a relay hunger strike against their 84-day suspension over protests held on the campus on August 13 this year, received the High Court order with tears of joy as slogans filled the air. CPI(M) district secretary S. Satish marked the end of the 22-day relay hunger strike by serving them lemon juice.

The suspended students were then taken to the SSUS campus in a triumphant march carrying a banner that read, “The people united will never be defeated,” an English translation of the Spanish slogan “¡El pueblo unido, jamás será vencido!”, which originated in Colombia in the 1940s and later became a global protest chant. SFI State president M. Sivaprasad and secretary P.S. Sanjeev accompanied the students.

“After trying to destroy our academics and careers, Higher Education Minister Roji M. John had sarcastically asked us to return to classes. Yes, we are now going back to our classes,” said P.S. Archana, one of the suspended students. “This is the victory of justice. No matter what happens, the truth will eventually come out,” she said.

“Even if we lose in life, we will never surrender before the RSS [Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh]. The verdict brings an end to the hardships that the 16 of us were subjected to. We will now enter the campus and write our examinations,” said M.S. Sivakumar, a second-year MA Theatre student, after ending his hunger strike.

“The Higher Education Minister, the Chief Minister, the vice-chancellor and the State government, all of whom targeted us and tried to disrupt our academics, should apologise. There was no need for us to apologise in the first place because we had committed no offence. This is the victory of the SFI against the combination of KSU [Kerala Students Union], the RSS and vice-chancellor Ciza Thomas,” another suspended student said.

Mr. Satish said that the politics behind vice chancellor Ciza Thomas’s unprecedented move to approach the court to prevent her own students from writing their examinations had now been exposed. The RSS project had been defeated, he said. He added that what began as a students’ struggle ceased to be theirs alone once secular and democratic sections of society rallied behind them after recognising the alleged RSS agenda. It evolved into a fight against what he described as the RSS line being pursued by the Chief Minister, V.D. Satheesan and Roji M. John, he said.
“We have ensured the defeat of Ciza Thomas. Roji M. John could have ended this protest on the very first day but instead adopted anti-people and anti-student positions,” said Mr. Sanjeev.

The Syndicate meeting held on November 2, 2026, which approved the findings of its five-member subcommittee probing the incidents of August 13, concluded that SFI activists had staged a mock funeral of vice chancellor Ciza Thomas. It stated that the involvement of the suspended students had been established through CCTV footage examined by the officials concerned.

The agitating students rejected the allegations, maintaining that they had merely staged a performance to draw attention to damaged lighting equipment in the Department of Theatre. The university authorities, however, rejected their claim that the equipment used during the August 13 protest comprised damaged lights belonging to the department. According to the authorities, the Head of the Department had informed the Syndicate that the lights were damaged during the 2018 floods. The university also noted that it had not received any complaint regarding damaged lights between 2018 and March 2026.

The SFI State leadership, meanwhile, issued a statement urging cultural activists across the State to speak out against the suspension of the 16 students. It alleged that the university authorities had denied the suspended students permission to write their examinations despite a directive from a Single Bench of the Kerala High Court. Actor and activist Prakash Raj had earlier visited the protesting students in solidarity.

articles.title: Bengaluru Namma Metro records 12.29% growth in ridership; fare revenue jumps 49% to ₹1,125 crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The annual report also highlighted the contribution of multiple digital ticketing options, including tokens, Smart Cards, QR tickets, National Common Mobility Cards (NCMC) and other digital payment platforms, towards improving passenger convenience and reducing transaction time at Metro stations.

The corporation recorded 310.49 million passenger journeys during 2025–26, compared with 276.51 million in the previous financial year. The average daily ridership increased to 8.51 lakh passengers from 7.57 lakh, registering a growth of 12.42%.

Namma Metro also recorded its highest-ever single-day ridership of 10.82 lakh passengers on August 14, 2025. On the same day, fare-box revenue reached ₹4.58 crore, setting a new single-day record for the corporation.
ALSO WATCH Namma Metro Pink Line: Will it ease traffic congestion? | Decode Karnataka

The increase in passenger numbers translated into higher ticket revenue. BMRCL generated ₹1,125.58 crore through fare-box collections during 2025–26, compared with ₹753.59 crore in 2024–25, marking a growth of 49.36%.
Non-fare revenue also witnessed significant growth, increasing to ₹88.51 crore from ₹54.97 crore in the previous financial year, registering a rise of 61.02%, according to the annual report.

The corporation attributed the growth in fare-box collections primarily to higher passenger ridership following the commissioning of the 19.15-km Reach-5 Yellow Line between RV Road and Bommasandra in August 2025.

BMRCL reported that trains operated with a punctuality rate of 99.85% during the financial year. Services commenced at 5 a.m. on Mondays to cater to passengers travelling early in the morning, while the last train services operated until 11.30 pm.

The corporation also reported an operational profit of ₹417.42 crore and a cash profit of ₹209.66 crore during 2025–26. According to the report, the expenditure during the year, excluding depreciation and finance costs, stood at ₹823.69 crore.

The annual report highlighted the contribution of tokens, Smart Cards, QR tickets, National Common Mobility Cards (NCMC) and other digital payment platforms, towards improving passenger convenience and reducing transaction time at Metro stations. | Photo Credit: The Hindu

BMRCL has been exploring additional revenue sources through commercial activities across its network. These include leasing station spaces , train and station advertising , outdoor advertisements , parking facilities and electric vehicle charging and battery-swapping stations.
During the year, the corporation earned ₹88.51 crore through non-fare revenue, compared with ₹54.97 crore in the previous financial year.

articles.title: Ukraine says Russian strikes kill 15 in Kyiv region
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year

Rescuers in Ukraine raced on Monday (November 23, 2026) to find residents trapped under the rubble of a block of flats that partially collapsed in a Russian strike, a fter attacks on the Kyiv region killed at least 15 people.
Moscow has been pummelling Ukraine with nightly aerial barrages as the war-torn country braces for another winter, as the full-scale invasion grinds through its fifth year.
Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed last week a "painful" response to Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Crimea bridge after holding a summit with U.S. counterpart Donald Trump and China's Xi Jinping.

An overnight strike on Dymer, around 45 kilometres (30 miles) north of the Ukrainian capital, hit a five-storey building, killing at least 11 people, according to Kyiv regional official Tymur Tkachenko.
AFP images showed rescuers combing through the mound of smouldering rubble.
"Rescuers recovered the body of another person from beneath the rubble," Tkachenko wrote on Telegram, confirming the death toll had risen to 11.
Ukraine's State Emergency Service said earlier on Telegram that the dead included a teenager and a woman in her forties.
It said earlier that rescuers were searching for 11 people, including two children, who were "not responding or cannot be reached".
Rescuers had managed to pull out people from the rubble including a 79-year-old woman and a child, Tkachenko said.
Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets called the attack part of "Russia's genocidal war against Ukraine".
"The world must stop looking away. Condemn this terror, hold Russia accountable, and act now to stop the killing of innocent Ukrainians," he said on X.
A Russian strike on a supermarket killed three other people and wounded 15, including three children, in Vyshneve, mayor Illya Dikov wrote on Facebook.

articles.title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to undertake official visit to Russia
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to undertake his first official visit to Russia, followed by a trip to Iran for a regional summit.
The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements, reported Dawn .

During his meeting with Russian President Vladi­mir Putin, discussions are expected to focus on ene­rgy cooperation, defence, trade, regional security and investment, a source in the Prime Minister’s Office told Dawn.
The revival of Pakistan Steel Mills, established with Russian assistance, is also likely to feature prominently, alongside potential Russian investment in Pakistan’s oil and gas sectors.

The two countries are likely to examine possibilities for Russian cooperation in restoring the industrial facility, alongside broader initiatives aimed at supporting Pakistan’s industrial development.
Later, Prime Minister Shehbaz will be travelling to Iran for the 18th Economic Coo­peration Organisation (ECO) Summit from December 3-4, according to Dawn .
Leaders of 10 member States will discuss regional trade, connectivity, energy, transportation, investment and industrial cooperation.
The summit comes ahead of Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit comes ahead of Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27.

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: Balen Shah begins bilateral visit; energy, connectivity on agenda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: This is Shah's first official bilateral foreign visit since taking office in March. He travelled to the U.S.; in September to attend the United Nations General Assembly
Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that India maintained supply of fuel and other essential goods to Nepal despite serious challenges related to oil supplies this year.
India and Nepal are partners in each other’s progress and source of support for each other in difficult times, he said.
The relationship between the two countries is not merely that of neighbours, but is reflective of unbreakable trust and friendship, he added.
Describing the rail service as a gift that would bring Awadh and Mithila closer, Mr. Adityanath extended his heartfelt congratulations to devotees of Lord Ram.
Nepal PM Balendra Shah said the talks between the two countries were aimed at further strengthening and modernising centuries-old Nepal-India ties.
As dependable neighbour, India consistently stood as first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult time in Nepal, he added.
Mr. Shah also said ties between India and Nepal stand as firm as the Himalayas and as vast as oceans.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi offered a $1.6 billion “development cooperation” package to neighbouring Nepal today in the wake of devastating Himalayan floods.

“To support Nepal’s reconstruction, and give fresh momentum to its long-term development, we announce a development cooperation package worth 240 billion Nepali rupees,” Mr. Modi said, standing alongside his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.

articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended setting up a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, contending that China may turn the process into an international contest over legitimacy.

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest.

The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in a report to the U.S. Congress, made a strong pitch to recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole legitimate authority to identify and recognise the successor to the 14th Dalai Lama.
The report by the bipartisan Commission said China was likely to use coercive tools to shape the outcome of the succession process.
It said that the U.S. Congress should adopt a policy of not recognising any successor to the Dalai Lama who is selected or installed by China.

“To carry out this policy and ensure U.S. government readiness for the Dalai Lama’s succession, Congress should direct the Secretary of State to… establish a senior-level channel with the Government of India for succession contingency planning, including intelligence sharing on Chinese influence operations,” the report said.

It also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to lead an internal interagency tabletop exercise on succession scenarios, with participation by the National Security Advisor, the Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defence.

The commission also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to conduct Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues and tabletop exercises with Indian counterparts on the political and security implications of succession scenarios.
The Commission also wanted the U.S. to coordinate with allies and partners on a diplomatic response that denies international legitimacy to any successor selected by China.

It also wanted the U.S. to counter succession-related influence operations by strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration’s cybersecurity and resilience against China’s cyber and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled disinformation campaigns.
Set up by the Dalai Lama in 2011, the Gaden Phodrang trust will have the sole authority to recognise his future reincarnation.

articles.title: Suspected Ukrainian sea drones hit Russian warship at Benghazi naval base, Libyan officials say
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said

A suspected Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship on Sunday (November 22, 2026) at a naval base in Libya, officials said, the latest attack in the North African nation linked to the Russia-Ukraine war.
The strike at the Benghazi Naval Base in eastern Libya severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette, and ignited a fire at the facility, two Libyan military officials said.

They said that several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship from a base run by Ukrainian forces in western Libya, according to an initial investigation into the attack. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, they said.
The officials, affiliated with the self-styled Libyan National Army, which controls eastern and southern Libya, spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't allowed to talk with reporters.

Libya has been divided since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime dictator Muammar Gaddafi, who was later killed, in 2011. A UN-supported government is based in Tripoli, and a rival administration is located in the east. The oil-rich nation remains a focal point for a long-running rivalry between Russia and the West.
The eastern Libya-based government said in a statement that the strike on Sunday (November 22) caused an explosion and fire at the base, which was later extinguished.

The Almasar satellite television channel aired footage showing a vessel erupting into flames. It said the Libyan navy rescued the crew of the Maltese-flagged ship. A corvette is a warship smaller than a frigate or destroyer and is built to patrol coastal waters and escort other ships.

The vessel had docked at the Libyan base for refuelling and supplies as part of a cooperation agreement between Russia and the eastern-based government in Libya, the statement said, without providing details on the vessel or its cargo.
A joint investigation was launched with Russia to “uncover the circumstances of the attack, its source, and the party behind it,” the statement said.
No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack. There was no immediate comment from either Russia or Ukraine.

A European official said the reports of an explosion at Benghazi Port involving a Russian vessel appeared to be credible. The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak on the record, said the vessel has been identified as a Russian corvette, adding they had no assessment of cause at this time.

On Sunday (November 22) evening, local media said that another sea drone hit a Maltese-flagged commercial vessel off the port of Benghazi in a separate attack. No further details were given. Almasar said that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.

articles.title: Alice Huang in touch with Chinese spy agency during affair with Nvidia CEO, says NYT
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment

Alice Huang, the Chinese woman at the heart of Nvidia’s recent scandal , kept in contact with an official ​from China’s top spy agency for more than a year during ‌her affair with former CEO Jensen Huang, the New York ​Times reported on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Alice Huang was in ⁠touch with an officer from China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the report said, ‌citing people with knowledge of intelligence reports that describe the encounters.
Spokespersons for Nvidia, Jensen Huang and the Chinese Embassy ‌in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for ‌comment. ⁠ Reuters has not been able to reach Alice ⁠Huang for comment.
Alice Huang previously led Singapore-based Megaspeed International, an important Nvidia customer that once accounted for billions in Nvidia chip sales.
U.S. authorities have been investigating Megaspeed ​since 2024 over concerns it smuggled ‌Nvidia’s advanced AI chips to China.
Sunday’s (November 22, 2026) report comes as US officials have cast doubt on initial suggestions that Alice Huang was a spy, as the newspaper reported last month.
That October ‌29 article touched off a scandal that led ​to Jensen Huang’s resignation two weeks later and a steep drop in Nvidia’s stock price.
Trump administration officials have ⁠repeatedly said they have not concluded that Alice Huang spied for China.
U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said this month the Justice Department ‌had not yet reached a conclusion on whether she was a Chinese spy.
U.S. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton repeated that on Sunday.

“Attorney General Blanche has been very clear that this is a matter under investigation, both Ms Huang and her company, for various matters,” Mr. Clayton told CNN’s “State of the Union” program. “And I’m ‌going to let that investigation play out.”

The scandal has also prompted a ​deeper look at Washington’s approach to export controls on China, with lawmakers from both parties questioning whether the ⁠Trump administration has been too lax on enforcement and regulation of the ⁠prized semiconductors.

articles.title: How to tune into world radio music from a single app
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Whether you’re yearning for futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a North Korean curation of classical symphonies, or just the sound of your own mother tongue, Radio Garden is a fantastic tool for listeners of all ages

If you listen to the radio while driving to work or doing the dishes, you’re probably familiar with five or so stations and regularly toggle between them in order to escape the ads. But imagine if you could point at almost any place on the map and tune into their radio offerings in real time. This is the premise of Radio Garden, which, in its own words, invites users to explore live radio around the world.

The process is simple: open the Radio Garden app or website to get to a Google Earth-like interface sprinkled with green dots, pick a radio station you’re interested in, and wait for it to load. If the station is available and responsive, you’ll soon be tuning into what locals are listening to.

Within a few minutes, a listener can explore futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a French curation of classical pieces, or the sound of their mother tongue as they imagine millions of others going about their day.
A screengrab of the Radio Garden user interface on web | Photo Credit: Radio Garden

Radio Garden has something for listeners of every age. Users can explore multiple available stations from the same place, or tour different cities. The local time is shown for each location, helping you get a sense of the kind of music you might hear there.

The Google Earth-inspired interface is a fantastic way to introduce children to geography and the concept of time zones, as well as expose them to new cultures and languages through music. It can also aid in learning languages through immersion.

The listening experience on Radio Garden is always unexpected; we enjoyed Chinese traffic updates and Columbian tunes for a while and were later surprised to hear a Pakistani radio station playing a popular Bollywood song. A Cairo radio station gently awakened sleepy listeners at sunrise with soothing romantic songs, while one in Pyongyang at the same time kept up post-lunch morale with fast-paced group duets.

Radio Garden also offers curated playlists from stations all over the world for those who prefer a more thematic and cohesive listening experience, regardless of whether they lean more towards religious chants or rock songs.

Furthermore, a fun ‘balloon ride’ game in Radio Garden randomly drops the listener right into a new place and starts playing the local radio station. It then slowly increases the viewer’s altitude to reveal more of the map, even as one races to guess which country’s music they are listening to.

The free version of Radio Garden comes with full-page visual ads that can be closed after a few seconds. We did not encounter any audio-based ads that interrupted our listening sessions, which is a major plus.

Radio Garden has been operated by Jonathan Puckey as an independent company since 2019, per its website. The Amsterdam-based team founded the project in 2016 when it was commissioned for a radio-themed exhibit. The team worked to upgrade and maintain the experience throughout the COVID-19 years.

“ By bringing distant voices close, radio connects people and places. From its very beginning, radio signals have crossed borders. Radio makers and listeners have imagined both connecting with distant cultures, as well as re-connecting with people from ‘home’ from thousands of miles away,” noted Radio Garden on its website.

This is the premise of Radio Garden, which, in its own words, invites users to explore live radio around the world.

The process is simple: open the Radio Garden app or website to get to a Google Earth-like interface sprinkled with green dots, pick a radio station you’re interested in, and wait for it to load. If the station is available and responsive, you’ll soon be tuning into what locals are listening to.

Within a few minutes, a listener can explore futuristic Russian pop, soulful Palestinian songs, a French curation of classical pieces, or the sound of their mother tongue as they imagine millions of others going about their day.

A screengrab of the Radio Garden user interface on web | Photo Credit: Radio Garden

Radio Garden has something for listeners of every age. Users can explore multiple available stations from the same place, or tour different cities. The local time is shown for each location, helping you get a sense of the kind of music you might hear there.

The Google Earth-inspired interface is a fantastic way to introduce children to geography and the concept of time zones, as well as expose them to new cultures and languages through music. It can also aid in learning languages through immersion.

The listening experience on Radio Garden is always unexpected; we enjoyed Chinese traffic updates and Columbian tunes for a while and were later surprised to hear a Pakistani radio station playing a popular Bollywood song. A Cairo radio station gently awakened sleepy listeners at sunrise with soothing romantic songs, while one in Pyongyang at the same time kept up post-lunch morale with fast-paced group duets.

Radio Garden also offers curated playlists from stations all over the world for those who prefer a more thematic and cohesive listening experience, regardless of whether they lean more towards religious chants or rock songs.

Furthermore, a fun ‘balloon ride’ game in Radio Garden randomly drops the listener right into a new place and starts playing the local radio station. It then slowly increases the viewer’s altitude to reveal more of the map, even as one races to guess which country’s music they are listening to.

The free version of Radio Garden comes with full-page visual ads that can be closed after a few seconds. We did not encounter any audio-based ads that interrupted our listening sessions, which is a major plus.

Radio Garden has been operated by Jonathan Puckey as an independent company since 2019, per its website. The Amsterdam-based team founded the project in 2016 when it was commissioned for a radio-themed exhibit. The team worked to upgrade and maintain the experience throughout the COVID-19 years.

“ By bringing distant voices close, radio connects people and places. From its very beginning, radio signals have crossed borders. articles.title: How long is too long on the throne?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: While there is no single magic number of minutes that is just the right amount of time to sit on the toilet, the broad agreement is up to 5 minutes. Scrolling your phone while sitting for long stretches of time may increase your risk of haemorrhoids

Every time I called my cousin Arun* around 9 a.m., his voice would echo, as though he were in a bathroom. “I’m on the throne, I’ll call you in 20 minutes,” he would say. The first time I heard this, it took me a while to understand what ‘the throne’ was, and as if that was not confusing enough, what was he doing there for 20 minutes. Perplexed, I asked him why he had the phone in the bathroom when he was doing his morning business, to which he casually replied that he would sit on the throne solving Wordle, crosswords and reading the news until he ‘downloaded’. A couple of months ago he told me that he was diagnosed with early stages of haemorrhoids and was on treatment. I advised him on this matter, stressing how his morning ritual could be contributing to his condition. This ultimately led to his ‘conscious reduction of phone time in the bathroom’. His words, not mine. Recently, he proudly announced that his scheduled ‘throne time’ was now down to six minutes, every morning after breakfast.

Bathroom humour is universal. Cinema is no exception — it has found humour and dependable plotlines from this predictable ritual. Just one instance is in Lokesh Kanagaraj’s Vikram , where a character pulling the flush coincides with the house exploding. Thankfully, the consequences of spending 20 minutes on the toilet are far less dramatic.

articles.title: In search of skin lightening creams, kidneys take a hit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Researchers from Kerala have reported a series of cases from Malappuram district where the regular use of fairness creams has been linked to nephrotic syndrome. Heavy metal screening of the blood and urine samples of these patients revealed high levels of mercury, the toxic effects of which are well-known

On the heels of recent news reports on how keratin-based hair-straightening products containing glycolic acid derivatives led to severe kidney injury in women, researchers from Kerala have reported a series of cases wherein, the use of fairness creams has been linked to nephrotic syndrome.

In a study published in the latest issue of Kidney International (‘NELL-1 associated membranous nephropathy linked to skin fairness cream use — insights from an Indian case series’, ) doctors describe a series of 15 cases of Membranous Nephropathy, reported by Aster MIMS Hospital, Kottakkal, Malappuram district, that were traced to the regular use of fairness creams.

Heavy metal screening of the blood and urine samples of these patients revealed high levels of mercury, the toxic effects of which are well-known. An analysis of the fairness creams also showed that these contained high levels of mercury -- in some instances, 10,000 times above the permissible limit of 1 ppm.

Since 2021, Ranjith Narayanan, a nephrologist practising at two busy private hospitals in Kozhikode, had noticed a specific pattern in cases of membranous nephropathy diagnosed amongst his patients. They all had non-specific symptoms — fatigue, mild edema and frothy urine — but high levels of proteinuria, in the range of 6.5-22.2 g/day.

articles.title: Medicos warn against craze for fairness after 17-year-old Keralam girl diagnosed with kidney disorder
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early
The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs.

A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her.

The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources.

Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early.

Warning against following social media beauty trends and using topical creams seen online or bought over the counter without a prescription, M.M. Faizal, former president of the Indian Association of Dermatologists, Venereologists and Leprologists, says people lack awareness of how topical applications can enter the bloodstream.

“People are obsessed with fair skin. We have observed a rise in the number of people buying steroid creams that are easily available over the counter and applying them to their faces. Such steroid-based applications and creams containing heavy metals such as mercury can damage your kidneys easily. The government needs to bring in some mechanisms to control this,” he says.

A rise in the number of teenagers relying on spurious beauty products has forced the Keralam Drugs Control department to launch awareness campaigns targeting students in Classes XI and XII, an age group particularly vulnerable to online campaigns. Frequent inspections are carried out in marketplaces to confiscate spurious cosmetics.
State Drugs Controller K. Sujith Kumar says raising awareness about such spurious cosmetic products is the only way forward.
“We have seized cosmetics that have high mercury levels from offline markets. But there is no way to track or regulate online marketplaces,” he says.

Prolonged use of such creams can lead to kidney damage, says former secretary of the Nephrology Association of Kerala, Jayant Thomas Mathew, who has come across a few cases of kidney disorders among users. The condition could be detected early because the patients were aware of the symptoms.

“The patients had used fairness creams and noticed symptoms related to kidney disorders. They probably had membranous nephropathy, and since they sought medical help at a very early stage, treatment was possible,” says Dr. Mathew.
Swelling in the legs and face and frothing in the urine are some of the signs people need to be wary about, the doctor adds.

articles.title: Bisleri says it’s water ‘safe for consumption’ after FSSAI sanctions prosecution, says it has received no notice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The company said five of six samples collected from its Goa facility in September 2025 met applicable standards, while an independent test found the bromate level in the disputed sample within the prescribed limit

Bisleri International has maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption, disputing the findings of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has sanctioned prosecution against the company after a water sample was declared unsafe following laboratory tests.

In a statement issued on Monday (November 23, 2026), the company said the matter related to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility, one of 143 plants in its network, and dated back about 14 months.

Bisleri said the FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025, of which five met all applicable standards. The sixth sample recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.

Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the FSSAI referred the sample to a referral laboratory for retesting. Bisleri said the referral laboratory found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit, but separately flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

The findings came after the initial laboratory examination had found the sample non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits, and declared it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The referral laboratory also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of PAHs. Based on the laboratory findings, the FSSAI subsequently sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri.

Questioning the differing test results, Bisleri said the difference between the two sets of findings raised questions that it believed warranted clarification. The company said it arranged for the same sample to be tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, where the bromate level was also found to be within the prescribed limit.
Bisleri said it submitted the independent test results to the FSSAI’s Western Regional Office along with a formal letter dated February 2, 2026.

“We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed. To date, Bisleri has received no notice by email or in hard copy and has been unable to locate the reported notice on FSSAI’s website,” a company spokesperson said.

The company’s management is deciding on the next steps, the spokesperson said. The company said it maintained stringent quality controls, including more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process. It added that it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI and address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process.

Bisleri International has maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption, disputing the findings of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has sanctioned prosecution against the company after a water sample was declared unsafe following laboratory tests.

In a statement issued on Monday (November 23, 2026), the company said the matter related to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility, one of 143 plants in its network, and dated back about 14 months.

Bisleri said the FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025, of which five met all applicable standards. The sixth sample recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.

Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the FSSAI referred the sample to a referral laboratory for retesting. Bisleri said the referral laboratory found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit, but separately flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

The findings came after the initial laboratory examination had found the sample non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits, and declared it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The referral laboratory also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of PAHs. Based on the laboratory findings, the FSSAI subsequently sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri.

Questioning the differing test results, Bisleri said the difference between the two sets of findings raised questions that it believed warranted clarification. The company said it arranged for the same sample to be tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, where the bromate level was also found to be within the prescribed limit.

Bisleri said it submitted the independent test results to the FSSAI’s Western Regional Office along with a formal letter dated February 2, 2026.

“We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed. To date, Bisleri has received no notice by email or in hard copy and has been unable to locate the reported notice on FSSAI’s website,” a company spokesperson said.

The company’s management is deciding on the next steps, the spokesperson said. The company said it maintained stringent quality controls, including more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process. It added that it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI and address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process.

articles.title: Lakshmi Aparna sworn in as Guntur Mayor; JSP’s Rajesh is Deputy Mayor
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Mayor promises to remain accessible to citizens and address their grievances through coordination between elected representatives and officials

Kovelamudi Lakshmi Aparna of the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) was sworn in as the new Mayor of the Guntur Municipal Corporation on Monday (November 23, 2026). Ward 64 corporator Yarramsetti Rajesh of the Jana Sena Party (JSP) was unanimously elected Deputy Mayor at the ceremony.
District Collector and Presiding Officer C.M. Saikanth Varma administered the oath of office to the Mayor and all 76 corporators, who attended the ceremony.

Subsequently, Mr. Rajesh was elected Deputy Mayor after his candidature was proposed by Ward 24 corporator Nimmala Venkata Ramana and seconded by Muthineni Rajesh and Irri Sai, corporators representing the 45th and 6th wards, respectively. Since there were no other candidates, the Presiding Officer declared him unanimously elected.

Addressing the gathering, Ms. Aparna said her priority was to ensure basic infrastructure for every household and make the civic body one of the best municipal corporations in the country. She promised to remain accessible to citizens and address their grievances through coordination between elected representatives and officials.
The Collector congratulated the newly elected representatives and assured the district administration’s full cooperation in the city’s development.

MLCs Alapati Rajendra Prasad and Chandragiri Yesuratnam, MLAs Nazeer Ahmed, Galla Madhavi and Burla Ramanjaneyulu, Jana Sena district president Gade Venkateswara Rao and Municipal Commissioner Mayur Ashok attended the ceremony.

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced

“As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees, expressed his condolences over the loss of lives in the Nepal floods.

PM Modi announced that India will establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Nepal, alongside a startup incubator and an innovation hub, as part of a broader push to empower Nepali youth and deepen bilateral educational and technological cooperation.

“Friends, Nepal’s youth generation is full of talent, energy, and big dreams. India is fully committed to partnering in making their dreams a reality. To realise this resolve, we will establish a startup incubator, an innovation hub, and an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology in Nepal,” PM Modi said.

Alongside setting up the IIT offshore campus, the Prime Minister announced expanded academic avenues in India for students from the Himalayan nation, stating, “We will expand scholarship opportunities in India for Nepali students in law and technology.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a development package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees for Nepal after holding wide-ranging talks with his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah that produced many key outcomes to further solidify the bilateral ties.

Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah warmly welcomed Indian investors to Nepal and called for translating bilateral understandings and infrastructure milestones into tangible gains for farmers, youth, students, and entrepreneurs across both countries.

“We are clear that the outcomes of the understandings that we reached today, and the projects we advance, must translate into prosperity in the fields of our farmers, employment and opportunity in the hands of our youth, new horizons in the dreams of our students, and tangible avenues for new markets, investment, and business expansion for our entrepreneurs. I am confident that these historic milestones will elevate Nepal-India relations to new heights. The need of the hour is to stand on the sturdy foundation of this enduring bond,” he added.
India will establish an offshore campus of IIT, expand scholarship opportunities in Law and Technology for Nepali students in India, says PM Modi.
The Prime Minister underscored New Delhi’s role in keeping fuel, fertiliser, and other essentials flowing to Nepal under its “Neighbourhood First” approach despite supply pressures this year.

“In keeping with our ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy, despite severe challenges in oil supply this year, we maintained uninterrupted supplies of fuel, fertiliser, and other essential goods to Nepal. Today, the dedication of Phase II of the Motihari–Amlekhgunj pipeline and the foundation stone laying for the Jhapa petroleum terminal will further strengthen this partnership,” he stated.
The energy and fuel initiatives were unveiled alongside a Joint Vision Document aimed at advancing shared goals of “Viksit Bharat” and “Samunnat Nepal” he added.

articles.title: India moving towards authoritarian rule through erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Ansari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Along with former Vice President Hamid Ansari, CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby, economist Prabhat Patanaik spoke at a seminar titled ‘The new age of imperialism’ organised by Sitaram Yechury foundation
India is facing challenges on several fronts which includes a gradual movement towards an authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions, former Vice-President Hamid Ansari said.

Mr. Ansari, through a video message, at a seminar organised by the Sitaram Yechury Foundation at Kolkata’s Pramod Dasgupta Bhawan, highlighted three point challenges faced by the country, which includes the pursuit of neoliberal policies, sharpening of communal polarisation and the movement towards authoritarian rule.

“This threefold attack includes the aggressive pursuit of neoliberal policies of economic reforms. Secondly, the relentless onslaught on the secular democratic foundations of the Indian republic by sharpening of communal polarisation, and thirdly, the movement towards authoritarian rule through the erosion of democratic institutions and methods of which are considered sacrosanct in a democracy,” the former Vice-President said.
From Sept 2026: Former V-P Hamid Ansari’s remarks exposed ‘Muslim League-Maoist character’ of Congress, says BJP

Recalling the contribution of the late Sitaram Yechury. Mr Ansari said that the CPI(M) spoke against the certain ideological position in which nationalism has only been equated with Hindu nationalism.

“Bharat Mata has no Hinduism in naturalism. This is not a Bharat Mata that has given birth to Muslims, Christians, Tarsus, Buddhists, Jains, and atheists,” Mr. Ansari quoted Mr. Yechury from one of his speeches in 2017.

The former Vice-President also said Mr. Yechury opined that the struggle against imperialist aggression, the imposition of neoliberal order, and fundamentalism should be welded together to form a powerful anti-imperialist movement. He emphasised the need to maintain multilateralism in external affairs so as not to compromise on foreign policy positions,

Mr. Ansari recalled that Mr. Yechury, despite some frictions within the CPI(M) and with the Congress, formed a strong relationship with the Congress leadership, particularly with Sonia Gandhi and the leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi. He was assisted in this by P. Chidambaram, who was a co-architect of the National Common Minimum Program of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government.

He viewed this programme not only as a revolutionary post-capitalist document but more as a social democratic agenda. “The CPI(M) and the Left Front wanted to be the watchdog of the new government. This is usually strange. The Congress accepted many of the suggestions to ensure a working majority,” he added.

Meanwhile, general secretary of CPI(M) M.A. Baby, Cuban Ambassador to India Juan Carlos Marsan Aguilera, renowned economist Prabhat Patnaik, historian Mukul Kesavan, and distinguished scholar Malini Bhattacharya were also present in the seminar in Kolkata on Sunday (November 22, 2026).

Addressing the seminar, Mr. Baby said that imperialism has reached a diabolical and barbaric stage across the world today. “Before Israel was to launch an attack on Iran without any rhyme or reason, the Prime Minister of India goes to Israel and addresses the Israeli Parliament two days ahead oftime. This is where we are living,” he said, recalling the Left parties’ struggle against the aggressive expansion of imperialism.

In his lecture, Mr. Patnaik discussed the current problems of capitalism, and called capitalism the basis of imperialism. He said that imperialism now looks so desperate and is causing an international crisis for which we still don’t have a clear answer. But he viewed the problems of capitalism are reasons behind such desperation.

He was assisted in this by P. Chidambaram, who was a co-architect of the National Common Minimum Program of the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government.

He viewed this programme not only as a revolutionary post-capitalist document but more as a social democratic agenda. “The CPI(M) and the Left Front wanted to be the watchdog of the new government. But he viewed the problems of capitalism are reasons behind such desperation.

articles.title: CPI(M) hails Kerala High Court relief to protesting Sanskrit University students as a slap in the face to the VC and UDF government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: M.V. Govindan said the High Court directive to conduct special examinations for the striking students, all hailing from working-class families, was a moral win for students’ rights and democracy

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the Kerala High Court’s order quashing the suspension of 16 students of Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in Kalady was a “resounding slap in the face” to Higher Education Minister Roji M. John and the varsity vice-chancellor (Dr. Ciza John).

CPI(M) State Secretary M.V. Govindan told reporters that Mr. John had actively aided the vice-chancellor, whom he portrayed as a Sangh Parivar enabler, to suspend the students, all Student Federation of India (SFI) activists, and deny them their right to appear for examinations. “Mr. John had revealed his true political colours. He demanded the students apologise to the vice-chancellor or forfeit their future”, he said.

Mr. Govindan said Mr. John’s demand that the students apologise had jarred Keralam’s civil society. “His demand was a hark back to the tradition of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leaders to apologise to colonial rulers and to become their eager acolytes to sabotage India’s storied Independence Struggle. The students spurned Mr. John’s demand and shrugged off the vice-chancellor’s threats and fought for their political cause”, he said.

Mr. Govindan said the CPI(M) was loath to borrow the humiliating word, “apologise”, from Mr. John’s and the Sangh Parivar’s “shared lexicon”. “Instead, the CPI(M) is daring Mr. John to show the moral courage to admit he and his government had erred in playing second fiddle to the RSS-appointed vice-chancellor”, he said.

Mr. Govindan said the High Court directive to conduct special examinations for the striking students, all hailing from working-class families, was a moral win for students’ rights and democracy. “To Mr. John’s and the vice-chancellor’s chagrin, the High Court had also insulated the students from their joint and strident demand for an apology for a foisted offence”, he said.

He said Mr. John and the vice-chancellor had punished the students for demanding basic campus infrastructure, including the lack of lecturers and delay in awarding fellowships. “However, the High Court came to the students’ rescue”, he added.

articles.title: NCERT to probe complaints of blurred text in school textbooks, assures corrective action
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The council said it would initiate strict action against any printer found responsible, after a Supreme Court lawyer flagged printing defects in Class 10 textbooks

The National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) has taken cognisance of complaints regarding poor print quality in its textbooks, particularly concerns over blurred and unclear text in certain school books.

“NCERT has taken cognisance of the print-quality concern, is viewing it seriously and is examining it on priority. Strict action will be initiated against any printer found responsible. NCERT remains committed to providing clear, readable, student-friendly textbooks for every child,” the council said in a post on X on Monday (November 23, 2026).

The action comes after Vineet Jindal, a Supreme Court lawyer, highlighted alleged printing defects in Class 10 textbooks. “My son is in class 10, and after going through his NCERT textbook, I am deeply concerned about the quality of printing. The text is extremely small, blurred and poorly printed, making it difficult for students to read comfortably,” Mr. Jindal had said in a post on X.
“NCERT must understand that such poor-quality textbooks can cause unnecessary eye strain, headaches and other health concerns among school children,” he had said.

articles.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest ex-PM Hasina if she returns from India
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Dhaka expects India to honour the extradition treaty, as Sheikh Hasina’s planned December return fuels political tension and street violence

Bangladesh will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, a senior government Minister said, as her plans to come home in December 2026 fuel political tension and renewed street violence.

Dhaka is instead seeking Ms. Hasina’s extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024, and expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told Reuters.
India’s External Affairs Ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In April 2026, the Ministry said it was examining Bangladesh’s request to extradite Ms. Hasina.
Ms. Hasina faces a death sentence in Bangladesh, and her Awami League party is banned following the 2024 uprising that ended her long rule.

The United Nations has said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest. Ms. Hasina fled Dhaka in August 2024 as protests demanding her resignation swept the country. She has since sought a new passport and identity card ahead of a planned return in December, requests the government has rejected.

“As soon as she tries to enter Bangladesh, she will be arrested. And she will be taken to jail, and the law will take its course,” Ms. Obaed said in an interview on Sunday (November 22, 2026). “We would like India to honour the extradition treaty and return her as a convict, and the law will take its course. She (Ms. Hasina) will have to face the music.”

The standoff has brought Ms. Hasina’s Awami League supporters out on the streets. The party this month announced a week of protests and rallies in support of Ms. Hasina’s return, culminating in a nationwide lockdown on November 19, 2026.

Police have recorded dozens of crude bomb blasts and incidents of arson targeting vehicles in at least 28 districts over the past 10 days, with several police officers and civilians injured, according to local media. Ms. Obaed called the violence a survival tactic by Ms. Hasina’s “politically bankrupt political party.”
Khalid Mahmud Chowdhury, a senior Awami League official, said the current political establishment was responsible for the violence.

The Minister said there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring Ms. Hasina back, adding that Dhaka wanted balanced ties with New Delhi that did not compromise Bangladesh’s “dignity, self-respect and interests.” “India needs to decide what kind of foreign policy they need to adopt for Bangladesh,” Ms. Obaed said.

Dhaka is also stepping up diplomatic pressure on neighbouring Myanmar over the return of Rohingya refugees, after the UN’s highest court ruled that thousands of killings and widespread sexual violence by Myanmar’s security forces against the Muslim minority in 2017 amounted to State-sponsored genocide.
Myanmar has criticised the ruling by the International Court of Justice and said Rohingya would only be able to return “when situations permit”.

articles.title: Israel at an Inflection Point
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation

Three years after Hamas’s October 7 attack shattered the core security promise of the state, Israel has emerged from a consequential Knesset election that ended Benjamin Netanyahu’s governing majority. Israel at an Inflection Point , published by The Hindu Group , examines how decades of unchecked militarism, a rightward political shift, and the collapse of the peace process have brought the country to this critical juncture.

The e-book brings together incisive essays by leading scholars and experts to offer a realistic picture of the strategic and political landscape surrounding the Jewish nation. Tracing the arc from late-19th-century European Zionism and the 1948 establishment of Israel to the geopolitical shocks of 2026, it probes the central tension between military dominance and durable security.

Across its chapters, the book explores how post-October 7 trauma has hardened Israeli opposition to Palestinian statehood, why tactical battlefield successes and high-profile assassinations have failed to produce a decisive strategic victory, and how rising American public scepticism and regional realignments are testing Washington’s traditionally unconditional backing. It also unpacks New Delhi’s pragmatic “de-hyphenation” policy, as India deepens defence and economic ties with Tel Aviv while maintaining its institutional support for a two-state solution.

For readers seeking a deeper grasp of a rapidly shifting West Asia, Israel at an Inflection Point provides essential historical depth and geopolitical context. Read this e-book to examine the domestic fault lines reshaping Israeli polity, the global economic fallout of the conflict with Iran, and India’s delicate diplomatic balancing act in the region.
· The predicament of the state of Israel by Stanly Johny
· How Israel sees the Palestine question today by Sujata Ashwarya
· From Gaza to Iran: Israel’s forever wars since October 7 by Rajeev Agarwal
· The evolving dynamics of the U.S.–Israel special partnership by M.H. Ilias
· Changes and continuity in India–Israel relations by Bashir Ali Abbas

fullParagraphs: In a year of unprecedented climate disasters, a supercharged El Niño and as the world heads inevitably past 1.5 °C of warming, the EU and other nations said that the international process did not meet the moment

These texts have always been add-ons to the formal negotiation process. Countries have regularly agreed these political, overarching statements, particularly since the Glasgow meeting in 2021, but they are not a requirement.

Australia and Turkey proposed a compromise – no fossil fuel language in exchange for support for electrification “with the greatest possible use of clean energy”.
This seemed to get Saudi Arabia over the line but drew backlash from the European Union, Panama, the Marshall Islands, Vanuatu, and Belize, who rejected the cover text.
