articles.title: Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s
Children who lived in Brazilian neighbourhoods buzzing with a special kind of mosquito were far less likely to catch dengue or another worrisome virus, chikungunya, researchers reported Saturday.

The major study of more than 5,700 children in one of the world's dengue hot spots offers new evidence that breeding mosquitoes unable to transmit these viruses can be a viable strategy rather than solely relying on pesticides and trying to avoid getting bitten.

In neighbourhoods populated by these so-called Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, researchers found about a 69% reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections in schoolchildren compared to similar neighbourhoods — an effect sustained even during Brazil's severe 2024 dengue outbreak, said Dr. Sri Edupuganti of Emory University, part of the international research team.
The researchers reported the findings at a meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.

“This is really exciting,” said David Hamer, a global health expert at Boston University who wasn't involved with the Brazilian study. He predicts that pairing more use of these Wolbachia mosquitoes with existing steps to fight mosquito-borne disease could “knock dengue down to much lower levels” in many places.
The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s.

Usually in the continental US, dengue is found mostly in people who travelled internationally. But as of Friday, Florida health officials had tallied more than 650 locally acquired cases, about three-quarters of them in Hillsborough County, home to Tampa.
Outside the U.S., the nonprofit World Mosquito Program has pioneered the Wolbachia strategy.

How it works: Scientists breed mosquitoes to carry a kind of bacteria called Wolbachia. It is harmless to people and common in many insects, although not dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacteria dramatically reduce the mosquitoes' ability to transmit certain viruses. Female mosquitoes spread the bacteria to their offspring, so releasing enough of the specially bred insects — males and females — into an area allows Wolbachia to gradually become established in the local mosquito population.

Field trials and other studies in Indonesia and elsewhere have shown the strategy can significantly lower dengue diagnoses. But because people with mild symptoms may not be diagnosed, the new study in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, went further. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.

The four-year study compared children living in neighborhoods that all got the same pesticide and other mosquito-control interventions, but half were randomly assigned to have Wolbachia mosquitoes released into the area. There were too few cases of Zika to calculate if the special mosquitoes had any effect on that disease.

articles.title: Raghumurthy visits tribal hamlets, directs officials to address basic amenities
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Minister for Tribal Welfare T. Raghumurthy on Monday visited tribal hamlets in the Saragur and H.D. Kote taluks and inspected Maharshi Valmiki Tribal Residential and Ashram Schools to assess the problems faced by tribal communities.
Interacting with residents, the Minister said protecting the interests of tribal communities and ensuring their overall development remained a priority for the government.
He gathered information on the availability of basic amenities, including roads, drinking water, housing, electricity and healthcare facilities in the hamlets.
He directed officials to ensure adequate infrastructure and facilities in ashram schools and residential hostels to provide quality education to tribal children.
The Minister instructed officials to address the grievances of tribal residents promptly and ensure that all eligible beneficiaries received the benefits of various government welfare schemes.

Emphasising the need to address drinking water problems, he called for immediate remedial measures whenever borewells became dysfunctional, installation of community borewells wherever necessary and provisions for electricity or solar-powered facilities for borewells located inside forest areas.

He said government services and essential documents should be made easily accessible to tribal residents. “Officials should not cite excuses but respond to local issues and take necessary steps to resolve them,” he said.

Stressing the need for inter-departmental coordination, he directed officials to resolve issues related to Aadhaar and ration cards, land titles and RTCs (Record of Rights, Tenancy and Crops), and ensure that government benefits reached even residents of remote hamlets inside forest areas.

Director of the Tribal Welfare Department Ashok D.R., Joint Director Rajkumar, Assistant Director Srinivas and Integrated Tribal Development Project Coordination Officer Bharathi C.R., among others, were present.

articles.title: Over 4,100 children share ideas for a child-friendly Cyberabad
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: More than 4,100 children across Cyberabad have voiced their concerns and offered suggestions on making their neighbourhoods safer and more child-friendly, as part of an initiative by the Cyberabad Municipal Corporation (CMC) to bring young residents into urban planning.

The CMC, in technical partnership with UNICEF, conducted ward-level consultations on Sunday across all 76 wards, 16 circles and three zones under its jurisdiction. The initiative, ‘Listening to Children: Child-Friendly CMC’, gathered 4,122 responses from children.

Depending on the geographical spread of each ward, two to three trained resource persons were deployed, with a target of reaching at least 50 children in every ward. They visited public parks, playgrounds, schools, residential streets and community centres to interact with children and record their feedback.

The consultations were guided by a Child-Friendly Ward Checklist developed by UNICEF. It covered 12 key areas relating to children’s everyday lives, safety, environment and urban infrastructure. Questionnaires were provided in Telugu and English to allow children to share their views in the language they were comfortable with.
Children from across the corporation’s jurisdiction flagged issues in their neighbourhoods and suggested ways to improve their surroundings.
With the first phase of data collection complete, the CMC and its technical teams will move on to the next two phases, comprising questionnaire-based consultations and group discussions.

The feedback will be grouped thematically and translated into actionable municipal plans, including infrastructure development and other urban planning initiatives. Through the exercise, the corporation aims to make its planning and services more responsive to children’s needs and concerns.

articles.title: Karnataka: Tension in Haveri over sugarcane prices
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tension prevailed in Haveri when farmers stormed the Deputy Commissioner’s office after sugar factories refused to pay a base price of ₹3,600 per tonne for sugarcane on Monday. Farmers in Haveri had been protesting across the district for the past few weeks, demanding ₹3,600 per tonne and implementation of a profit-sharing formula.
District administration officials held a series of meetings with farmers and factory representatives, but failed to break the deadlock.

Farmers were demanding that the profit-sharing formula adopted in a meeting between farmers and sugar factories in Belagavi be implemented across the State. However, the factories argued that it was an agreement limited to Belagavi district.

Some factories said they could not pay even ₹3,000 per tonne. However, they accepted the profit-sharing formula on the condition that the Union government revise the Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar beyond ₹45 per kg. When word spread that factories were offering a maximum price of ₹3,100 per tonne, farmers became agitated and stormed the DC’s office. The police took some protesters into custody and released them later.

articles.title: NIT-C inks pact with IRFC Foundation to set up health centre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The project will strengthen healthcare infrastructure for the NIT-C community by providing accessible and affordable primary healthcare services to students, faculty and staff.

The National Institute of Technology-Calicut (NIT-C) has signed a memorandum of agreement with Indian Railway Finance Corporation (IRFC) Foundation, New Delhi, to construct a modern health centre on its campus. The project is under the corporate social responsibility scheme of the IRFC.

The agreement was signed by S. Kumaravel, Dean, International, Alumni and Corporate Relations, and Shwet Ketu Mishra, Member, IRFC Foundation. The foundation has committed up to ₹2 crore for the project titled ‘Shushrutha Swasthya Kendram’.

A release said on Monday (November 23) that the project would strengthen healthcare infrastructure for the NIT-C community by providing accessible and affordable primary healthcare services to students, faculty and staff. The centre is also expected to enable faster emergency response, reduce the need to travel for medical consultations, and improve campus preparedness for public health emergencies, including infectious disease outbreaks. The initiative is being undertaken with the support of the NIT Calicut Alumni Association.

articles.title: Police constable exam postponed in M.P.; Congress, CPI(M) slam BJP government
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: In a notification on the night of November 22, the Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board postponed the recruitment examination for 7,500 police constable posts, earlier tentatively scheduled to begin on November 19

The Congress and the Communist Party of India (Marxist) on Monday (November 23, 2026) slammed the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Madhya Pradesh after a police constable recruitment exam was postponed, accusing it of “playing with the future” of youth.

In a notification on Sunday night (November 22, 2026), the Madhya Pradesh Employees Selection Board postponed the recruitment examination for 7,500 police constable posts, earlier tentatively scheduled to begin on November 19.

“In the advertisement and rule book issued by the Board for “Direct Recruitment Selection Examination 2026 for Constable (GD) under Police Headquarters, Home (Police) Department, Government of Madhya Pradesh”, the tentative exam date “starting from 19/11/2026” was advertised. The candidates related to the said exam are informed that keeping in view the conduct of other exams of the Police Department itself and the interest of the candidates, the Board has postponed the exam date and the fixed date of the exam and the detailed time table (Exam Schedule) will be announced very soon on the official website,” the Board said.
Slamming the move, Congress MLA and Leader of Opposition in the Assembly Umang Singhar alleged that “the BJP government does not care about young people, only about advertisements”.

“What could be a bigger joke with young people’s futures in Madhya Pradesh? The police constable recruitment exam, due to begin on November 19, has now been postponed. Hundreds of thousands of candidates have been waiting for the exam after months of hard work, but the government cannot even hold it on time,” Mr. Singhar said.

Mr. Singhar claimed, “Unemployment in the state is so bad that for a post requiring only a 12th-grade education, 42 PhD holders, 12,000 engineers, 51,000 postgraduates, and 3,25,000 graduates are applying.”
“Mohan Yadav ji, stop playing games with young people’s futures,” he said, asking the Chief Minister to announce the new exam date immediately and complete the recruitment process.
CPI(M)’s State secretary Jaswinder Singh said that the delay in the exam affected 7.54 lakh candidates while terming it a “cruel joke” by the government.
Claiming that the examination was postponed suddenly without any valid reason, Mr. Singh said that the candidates had spent thousands of rupees at coaching centres and prepared for months.
“The youths in the state are being made to pay for the government’s inability to conduct examinations. The government must announce a fresh date for the examination without delay,” Mr. Singh said.

articles.title: Harassment alleged in Plus Two student’s suicide; kin protest with body
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: High drama and tense moments prevailed at the Sooranad Government Higher Secondary School on Monday as grieving relatives, local residents, and students staged a protest with the body of a 17-year-old Plus Two student, demanding strict legal action against the school authorities over allegations of severe mental harassment that drove him to suicide.

The deceased, identified as Niranjan, son of Santhosh and Raji of ‘Niranjana Nivas’ in Anayadi, Sooranad, was found dead at his residence around 3 a.m. on Sunday. Following the post-mortem examination at the Sasthamkotta taluk hospital on Monday morning, the family brought his body to the school gates, holding the institution responsible for his untimely death.

The family has leveled grave allegations against the school administration, claiming that the principal and teachers humiliated Niranjan in front of other students simply for speaking to a female classmate. According to the relatives, the authorities subsequently summoned the girl’s parents to the school office, subjecting the boy to severe mental distress that ultimately pushed him to end his life.

Student organizations joined the agitation alongside the bereaved family, raising slogans and demanding an impartial probe. Protesters insisted that investigators thoroughly examine the conduct of the teachers, recent incidents at the school, and the student’s mental state, calling for exemplary punishment if any lapses are proven.

The standoff ended only after people’s representatives, police officials, and education department authorities held conciliatory talks with the protesters. Following official assurances of a fair inquiry and strict legal action against anyone found guilty, the family agreed to disperse and proceed with the funeral rites.

Meanwhile, Niranjan’s relatives have lodged a formal complaint with the Sooranad police seeking a comprehensive investigation into the incident, with officials stating that detailed statements from the family, classmates, and school staff will be recorded soon.

Taking cognizance of media reports regarding the tragedy, the Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has also registered a suo motu case. The Commission has sought urgent, detailed reports from the Deputy Director of Education (DDE), the Sooranad Station House Officer (SHO), the District Child Protection Officer, and the school principal.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

“After the ninth New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) round was launched in 2010, no new exploration round was offered until 2016,” it added. “The fields producing today were not replaced by new ones in that period, and the effect is still being felt.”

The Ministry also stated that mature oil and gas fields generally lose 7-8% of their output every year as reservoir pressure falls and that most of India’s current production comes from such fields. On the other hand, new wells, enhanced recovery, and field redevelopment are making up much of the loss.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates

The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.

These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit highlights: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur.

Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’.
Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said.

Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship.

It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations.
Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.

“As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees, expressed his condolences over the loss of lives in the Nepal floods.

PM Modi announced that India will establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) in Nepal, alongside a startup incubator and an innovation hub, as part of a broader push to empower Nepali youth and deepen bilateral educational and technological cooperation.

“Friends, Nepal’s youth generation is full of talent, energy, and big dreams. India is fully committed to partnering in making their dreams a reality. To realise this resolve, we will establish a startup incubator, an innovation hub, and an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology in Nepal,” PM Modi said.

articles.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.
Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow.
"We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said.
"We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner."
European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks.

Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries.
He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies.
"NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering.
A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

"Not all NATO allies agree at this moment (on) letting Ukraine become a member," Mr. Rutte said, though he also firmly rejected the idea that outside powers like Russia could dictate who joins the alliance.

During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

Bangladesh’s garment manufacturers could propose a roughly 15% ​increase in the minimum monthly wage at talks with authorities on Monday (September 23, 2026), industry ⁠leaders said, far short of workers’ demands for more than double their pay.

articles.title: Study finds PTSD-specific brain changes, paving way for personalised treatment
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD

A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD.

Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a mental health disorder in which one experiences flashbacks or nightmares of a terrifying or life-threatening event.

The study, published in the journal ' Cell Reports' , also found that among people affected by PTSD, the molecular variations appeared to be driven by a number of factors, including the sex and race of the person, and whether the trauma exposure occurred in childhood or adulthood.
"The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said.

"The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said.
The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said.
A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder.

Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory.

The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.
PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.
The molecular patterns were associated with differences in the composition of different cell types in the brain, the researchers said.
Because they analysed postmortem brain tissue, the team was not able to confirm whether the methylation differences contributed to PTSD, resulted from PTSD, or were influenced by other factors.

articles.title: Rotary Club of Madras partners with Tamil Nadu government to vaccinate 3.5 lakh girls against HPV
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The club aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29

The Rotary Club of Madras (RCM) and the Tamil Nadu government have entered into a partnership to provide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 3.5 lakh adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer.

The partnership, valued at approximately ₹200 crore, is among the largest public-private initiatives for HPV vaccination in India. It was acknowledged in the presence of Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu government.

High-risk HPV infections account for more than 95% of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination during adolescence helps prevent infections caused by high-risk HPV types and reduces the risk of cervical cancer later in life.

Bobby Krishna, president of the Rotary Club of Madras, said the partnership was part of Rotary’s efforts to work with the government on large-scale vaccination programmes. The club also aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29, building on its work under the Polio Plus programme.

articles.title: Many children may be wearing spectacles with the wrong prescription. What does this mean for their vision?
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: The objective is not merely to ensure that children wear spectacles, but that the prescription is appropriate, the lenses are correctly dispensed and their vision is monitored as they grow

An incorrect or outdated spectacles prescription can leave a child’s vision inadequately corrected, affecting classroom activities and learning. Regular eye examinations are important because children’s eyesight can change as they grow, and wearing spectacles alone does not ensure that their vision is being corrected properly.

A study of 5,268 school-going children in north India found that only 23.03% of those prescribed spectacles were using the correct prescription. Inaccurate spectacle power was common, with younger age and longer duration of spectacle use among the associated factors.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Many children may be wearing spectacles with the wrong prescription. What does this mean for their vision?. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial

Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), a laser procedure used to correct vision. At six hours after surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving a placebo.
Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases. The company said there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways.

Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial. Shares of the eye-care company fell 1.4% in extended trading.

articles.title: Antimicrobial overuse could make common infections harder to treat: Health ministry official
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: World AMR Awareness Week is observed from November 18 to 24 every year to improve awareness and understanding of antimicrobial resistance and promote best practices among the public, policymakers and One Health stakeholders

Misuse and overuse of antimicrobials could undermine decades of medical progress and make even common infections increasingly difficult to treat, a senior health ministry official said on Wednesday, calling for collective action to contain antimicrobial resistance (AMR).

Addressing the national observance of World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week 2026 virtually, Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava described AMR as one of the most serious public health challenges and stressed the need for a coordinated "One Health" approach to tackle it.
This year's theme is "One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now".
She said medicines that have saved countless lives are gradually losing their effectiveness due to misuse and overuse.

Srivastava highlighted the interconnectedness of human and animal health, plant and food systems and the environment, noting that improper use of antimicrobials across these sectors contributes to the emergence and spread of resistance.

She said the government has accorded high priority to containing AMR, with the National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance 2.0 (NAP AMR 2.0), 2025-2029, providing a framework for surveillance, infection prevention, responsible antimicrobial use, research and coordinated action.

The health ministry's National Programme on AMR Containment, coordinated by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), focuses on strengthening laboratory capacity for AMR surveillance, infection prevention and control, antimicrobial stewardship and awareness generation, she said.

Srivastava urged healthcare professionals to prescribe antibiotics only when clinically indicated and in accordance with treatment guidelines. She also asked pharmacists to ensure appropriate dispensing against valid prescriptions and counsel patients on their correct use.

She also advised people against self-medication, sharing antibiotics or using leftover medicines, stressing that antibiotics are not effective against viral infections such as the common cold and influenza.
More than half of antimicrobial sales in India take place without prescriptions, while nearly half of outpatient antibiotic prescriptions are inappropriate, participants at the event noted.

They called for scaling up public awareness campaigns, preventing self-prescription, ensuring proper disposal of antibiotics and expired medicines, and displaying legal warnings at drug shops against the sale of antimicrobials without prescriptions.

Participants also stressed the need to curb production of substandard and spurious medicines, promote appropriate antibiotic use in veterinary medicine, particularly for food-producing animals, and maintain quality standards in healthcare facilities to prevent infections.

articles.title: National Children’s Theatre Festival concludes in Mysuru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The National Children’s Theatre Festival, jointly organised by the Jagannath Centre for Art and Culture (JCAC) and the Indian Institute of Educational Theatre (IIET), which began on November 15, concluded on Sunday.
Speaking at the valedictory ceremony, JCAC director Ravikumar said more than nine theatre troupes from different parts of the country staged plays under the guidance of eminent directors.

He emphasised the importance of providing children with platforms to showcase their talents, stating that theatre activities at the primary school level could contribute to their intellectual development and positively influence their learning and academic performance.
He also appreciated the efforts of JCAC and IIET in promoting children’s theatre and taking Mysuru’s cultural identity to a national audience.

The plays were staged at 12 schools across the city, including Hardwicke School, Government Pre-University College in Kuvempunagar, Mathrumandali School, Bachpan Play School, Hari Vidyalaya, Mahaveer Vidya Mandir, Arivu Vidya Samsthe, BSS Vidyalaya, Morarji Desai School in Salundi, Ican International School, Learning Curve International School, and Atomic Energy School. The performances received an encouraging response.

In his introductory remarks, Indian Theatre Foundation Trustee Jayaram Patil said eight prominent theatre personalities had been invited to the festival, and nearly 2,500 children had been introduced to theatre through performances organised at the 12 schools.

The participating artists and groups included Saraswathi and B.V. Shringa from Bengaluru, Shivaram and Sundaresh Devapriya from Mysuru, Seema Ghosh from West Bengal, the Classic Theatre Foundation from Maharashtra and Ujagar Dramatic Association from Mumbai. IIET’s production, Pippi Hindu Pappu , was also staged.
Arivu Samsthe’s Janardhan and several other dignitaries were present.

articles.title: Telangana HC orders ₹2 lakh compensation to woman, 24 years after husband’s death in police encounter
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Telangana High Court has ordered the State to pay ₹2 lakh in compensation to a woman whose husband was killed in a police encounter at Chegunta in Medak district in 2001.

Pronouncing the verdict on a writ petition filed in 2002 by Ponna Venkatamma, widow of Balanarsaiah, Justice Suddala Chalapathi Rao observed that the State had failed to follow the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) guidelines and investigate the encounter. The judge held that the police authorities concerned — the Sub-Inspector of Chegunta police station, Medak Superintendent of Police and Principal Secretary (Home) — “are liable to compensate the petitioner for the loss of her husband at the hands of the police”.

On October 10, 2001, the Sub-Inspector of Chegunta police station was abducted by Naxalites during a physical confrontation at Chetla Thimmayapalli. He was released the following day. The police subsequently named Balanarsaiah among nine villagers accused of being involved in the abduction.

On December 12 that year, Balanarsaiah was killed in an encounter with a police team that included Chegunta SI Kishen Singh. The police had claimed that he was a member of the Indupriyala Local Guerrilla Squad of the outlawed People’s War Group.

Appearing for the petitioner, counsel Vasudha Nagaraj argued that the NHRC had laid down guidelines as early as 2001 for dealing with deaths in “police encounters”. Under these guidelines, the State is required to register a case involving a cognisable offence and have the incident investigated by an independent agency such as the Crime Investigation Department (CID).

The judge observed that while the State authorities had registered cases against the extremists and the petitioner’s husband, they were legally bound to register a case against the police personnel involved in the encounter as well.

The facts of the case fell within the ambit of the NHRC guidelines of 1997, which the State had failed to follow, Justice Rao noted. Despite the prescribed procedure, no investigation was conducted into the encounter, nor was any inquiry report placed before the court to establish whether Balanarsaiah’s death was the result of an act of self-defence.

However, the judge observed that directing the State to register an FIR and investigate the incident after such a long lapse of time would serve little purpose. The court, therefore, ordered the State to pay ₹2 lakh in compensation to the petitioner.

articles.title: Keralam CPI(M) constitutes commission to probe E.P. Jayarajan’s allegations against P. Jayarajan
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sources in the party say E.P. Jayarajan sought relief from the party over P. Jayarajan allegedly linking him to financial misdemeanour in connection with a resort, which he said had sullied his reputation

The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] Keralam State secretariat has constituted an internal inquiry commission to probe the allegations levelled by the party’s central committee member E.P. Jayarajan against State secretariat member P. Jayarajan.
The duo, the strongmen of the party in Kannur, have been locked in a bitter turf war, and the complaint is the latest development in a series of allegations they have hurled at each other.
The complaint will be examined by a party commission comprising central committee members K.N. Balagopal and T.P. Ramakrishnan.

Sources in the party said Mr. E.P. Jayarajan sought relief from the party over Mr. P. Jayarajan allegedly linking him to financial misdemeanour in connection with a resort, which he said had sullied his reputation. Mr. E.P. Jayarajan also accused the latter of associating with ‘quotation’ mafia and gold smuggling gangs and a resort in Idukki.

The commission, it is said, will look into all aspects of the allegations, including those against Mr. E.P. Jayarajan. The tug-of-war between the two has roiled the CPI(M) politics in the district for a few years now.
Mr. P. Jayarajan denied the allegations against him, terming them as ‘baseless’. He said he was not concerned about such charges and did not wish to offer any explanation.

articles.title: Food poisoning: 63 tourists treated at hospital in Idukki
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Sixty-three students and teachers sought treatment from hospital after showing symptoms of food poisoning after eating from a restaurant at Kattappana in Idukki on Sunday night.
The affected group had travelled to Idukki from a coaching centre in Malappuram. They arrived in Kattappana in four buses after visiting Kodaikanal.

According to officials, the group ate mandi at a restaurant in Kattappana around 10 p.m. on Sunday. About an hour later, at 11 p.m., 52 students experienced physical discomfort and sought treatment at Kattappana Taluk Hospital, while 11 students and teachers were treated at Idukki Medical College. After receiving primary care, the group returned to Malappuram on Monday morning.

Following the incident, the Kattappana municipal health wing inspected the restaurant, though no stale food was found. Health officials collected food samples from the establishment and handed them over to the Food Safety Department for testing.

Officials noted that because the tour group had eaten at several other restaurants in Nedumkandam and nearby areas earlier, the exact source of the food poisoning can only be confirmed once test results are returned. However, some members of the group said those who consumed mayonnaise at the restaurant were the ones affected.

articles.title: No Winter Session of Parliament? Skipped only four times in history
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Each previous instance coincided with extraordinary disruptions, from the Emergency and Lok Sabha dissolutions to Indira Gandhi’s assassination and the COVID-19 pandemic

The Winter Session of Parliament has been skipped only four times in India’s parliamentary history, and each instance was linked to exceptional circumstances, including the Emergency, the premature dissolution of the Lok Sabha, the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

With the Monsoon Session yet to be prorogued, setting a record for Parliament remaining unprorogued for more than 100 days, speculation has grown over the possibility of a short special session to consider the delimitation Bill.
The absence of any move to summon Parliament for its customary winter sitting has also fuelled discussion about whether the session could be skipped altogether.

The first time Parliament missed its winter session was during the 19-month Emergency. The Lok Sabha met from July 21 to August 7, 1975, and then only from January 5 to February 6, 1976, without sitting during November or December, when the Winter Session is normally held.
The next instance came in 1979 after the premature dissolution of the Sixth Lok Sabha on August 22. The newly elected House met only in January 1980, resulting in the Winter Session being skipped.

A similar situation arose in 1984 following the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on October 31. General elections were called, and the Eighth Lok Sabha held its first sitting on January 15, 1985.

After a gap of 36 years, the Winter Session was skipped again in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic. Amid fears over the spread of the virus and stringent social-distancing norms, Parliament did not meet after the truncated Monsoon Session that ran from September 14 to 23.
In the 12 years of the Narendra Modi government, the timing of the Winter Session has varied considerably.

On six occasions, it was convened in November; as early as November 16 in 2016 and as late as November 29 in 2021. On five occasions, it began in December, with start dates ranging from December 1 to December 15.

Article 85 of the Constitution, which deals with the summoning and prorogation of Parliament, does not prescribe the number of sessions to be held each year. It only mandates that the interval between two sessions cannot exceed six months.

The government is comfortably placed in the Rajya Sabha, where the BJP-led NDA has 151 members, compared with 64 for the INDIA bloc. According to sources, the government has also examined precedents where the Rajya Sabha was convened even when the Lok Sabha was not in session.

According to Rajya Sabha at Work , until 1961, the two Houses often commenced their sessions on different dates, except for the first session of the year or the first session after a general election.

articles.title: India, Nepal to hold 20th edition of joint military exercise Suryakiran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Exercise Suryakiran is a key bilateral military engagement between India and Nepal, providing an opportunity for the two armies to enhance interoperability, exchange operational experiences and strengthen coordination through joint training

India and Nepal are set to hold the 20th edition of their joint military exercise Suryakiran, aimed at further strengthening military cooperation and deepening the defence partnership between the two neighbouring countries.

The Indian Army announced the upcoming edition in a post on X, reaffirming the enduring military ties between the two countries. “The Indian Army and the Nepali Army are set to participate in the 20th edition of Joint Military Exercise Suryakiran, reaffirming the enduring partnership between the two neighbouring nations,” the post said.
The Army also described the exercise as a reflection of the close bond between the two countries, with the tagline, “Two Nations. One Mission. An Enduring Bond.”
The announcement comes after the successful conclusion of the 19th edition of Exercise Suryakiran in December 2025 at Pithoragarh in Uttarakhand.

The 19th edition culminated with a closing ceremony following an intensive combined training cycle at the Foreign Training Node in Pithoragarh. The Directors General of Military Operations (DGMOs) of the Indian Army and the Nepal Army jointly witnessed a two-day Battalion-level Validation Exercise conducted as part of the exercise, according to the Ministry of Defence.

Exercise Suryakiran is a key bilateral military engagement between India and Nepal, providing an opportunity for the two armies to enhance interoperability, exchange operational experiences and strengthen coordination through joint training.

articles.title: Zelenskyy hails Ukraine's attack on a Russian warship in Libya
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces

Ukraine carried out an attack on a Russian warship moored at a port in Libya, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday (November 23, 2026), claiming that maritime drones sank the navy vessel in a surprise assault the previous day.

Ukrainian forces deployed seven drones in the operation that struck the Russian navy corvette in the Mediterranean, according to Mr. Zelenskyy. The ship, the Merkury, was one of Russia's newest vessels, commissioned a year after Moscow launched the 2022 full-scale invasion of its neighbor, he said in a post on X.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to comment on the attack, saying that Russia's Defense Ministry would provide more information “if deemed to be appropriate.”
The operation, conducted some 2,400 kilometres (1,500 miles) from the front line in Ukraine, was the latest daring long-range assault by Kyiv's forces.

Ukraine has at times embarrassed Moscow during the war with attacks such as Operation Spiderweb in June 2025, when drones launched from trucks hit over 40 aircraft parked at air bases across Russia. Along the roughly 1,250-kilometre (almost 800-mile) front line snaking through eastern and southern Ukraine, Kyiv's drones and ground robots are helping hold back Russia's bigger army.
At the same time, Russia's missiles and drones have devastated Ukraine's power grid ahead of winter and damaged civilian buildings.

A Russian strike on a five-story apartment block in a village near Kyiv killed 11 people, regional police said on Monday (November 23, 2026). A 7-year-old child and a 79-year-old woman were pulled alive from the rubble after the Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning attack, rescue services said.

Three people were killed on Monday (November 23, 2026) in a Russian strike on a hospital in the city of Zaporizhzhia in southern Ukraine, the regional military administration said. Two other people were killed when Russian forces struck a vehicle that bore markings indicating it was evacuating residents from the eastern city of Kramatorsk, authorities said.
Mr. Zelenskyy described Sunday's (November 22, 2026) attack as “exemplary” and said “the targets we set were achieved.”
“We continue our operations in designated waters. We are responding to Russia's aggression. We are developing Ukrainian weapons,” he said.

Ukraine has hit Russian oil refineries as far away as western Siberia and Russian warships in the Mediterranean, Mr. Zelenskyy noted in a video address to a meeting of the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

An oil refinery in Russia's western Rostov region halted work on Monday (November 23, 2026) after what Gov. Yuri Slyusar said was a “massive” Ukrainian drone and missile attack that lasted more than six hours. Ukraine's General Staff said the refinery, located just a few dozen kilometres (miles) from the Ukrainian border, can process up to 55 million barrels of oil a year and was on fire after the attack.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.”

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement.
Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”
Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart".
Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused.
Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.
U.S. intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.

Board chair Harvey Jones said on Monday (November 23, 2026) that directors now believe Mr. Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers.

articles.title: Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Tech, Innovations & Ecology Reports
fullParagraphs: SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories

According to a survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), severe anaemia was observed in less than 2% of people in the majority of age groups. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 was released on Monday (November 23, 2026).

It showed that children aged 12-59 months had 42% anaemia prevalence, adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had anaemia prevalence of 46%, adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20–59 years had 22-23% anaemia prevalence, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence.
The survey also found that mild anaemia constitutes a substantial proportion of the overall anaemia burden.

“SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of anaemia across children, adolescents, adults, pregnant and lactating women and older adults, together with detailed information on micronutrient deficiencies to evaluate potential causes of anaemia. It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Rajiv Bahl, secretary, Department of Health Research.

The report noted that about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls, and children, have mild anaemia, indicating considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe anaemia. Anaemia prevalence is much lower among adolescent boys, adult and older men, and even among those affected, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, said the release issued by the Union Health Ministry.

SAMPADA represents one of the largest and most comprehensive nutrition surveys undertaken globally. The survey covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. SAMPADA findings show that iron deficiency is largely restricted to population groups including under-five children, adolescent girls, and women of reproductive age, while adolescent boys, men, and the elderly have a low prevalence of iron deficiency. articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Updates
fullParagraphs: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Will use 'all available means' to counter U.S. blockade: Iran
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
Iran said on Monday (November 23, 2026) it would use all means at its disposal to counter a U.S. naval blockade that was imposed in retaliation for its own push to block the Strait of Hormuz.
"We will certainly not tolerate these actions and will use all available means to counter U.S. aggression," said Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei in a weekly press briefing.
War broke out between Iran and the United States on February 28 when U.S.-Israeli strikes killed the Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.
The conflict has since expanded after Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes across the region, and with militant groups it backs in Lebanon, Yemen and Iraq also entering the fray.
The Strait of Hormuz has become the focus of the conflict, with Iran continuing in its efforts to blockade the waterway, vital to global energy supplies.
In response, the U.S. imposed its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. It later announced a raft of economic sanctions, and launched a task force to disrupt land routes into Iran.

"You should bear in mind that what the Americans have described as economic sanctions, an economic blockade and a naval blockade undoubtedly constitutes an act of military aggression against Iran," said Mr. Baqaei.
"Under these circumstances, Iran is entitled, pursuant to Article 51 of the UN Charter, to use any means at its disposal to defend itself."
Iranian forces have made multiple announcements in recent weeks of ships catching fire attempting to use routes that Tehran considers off-limits.
Diplomatic efforts to resolve the crisis remain stalled, especially since the collapse of a June deal that laid out a pathway to a permanent settlement.
Iran has said Hormuz could be open within two days but only if Washington agreed to its list of demands which include the lifting of the blockade.
"If the American side fulfils its commitments, security can be restored to the Strait of Hormuz and the region in the shortest possible time," Mr. said Baqaei.

articles.title: Armenia drops Nagorno-Karabakh claim in proposed new constitution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS) & Geopolitics
fullParagraphs: The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire

Armenian leader Nikol Pashinyan unveiled a draft constitution on Monday (November 23, 2026) that would get rid of a 1990 independence clause and claim to the disputed Karabakh region, saying it was the only way to reach a peace deal with Azerbaijan.
The Caucasus foes have been locked in a territorial conflict over the mountainous region since the fall of the Soviet Union.
In a 2023 offensive, Baku retook the Armenian-populated region, forcing a mass exodus, and has since demanded that Yerevan change its constitution for a peace treaty to be possible.
Mr. Pashinyan addressed Armenians, promising a peace treaty with Azerbaijan should his countrymen back the new constitution in a referendum.

Mr. Pashinyan said the new text rejects "the logic of the Declaration of Independence of August 23, 1990 — that is, the logic of conflict" and said the aim of the new constitution is to "ensure peace".

The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire.
Armenia's Opposition has accused Mr. Pashinyan of bowing to Azerbaijan's demands under pressure, calling it "Aliyev's Constitution" — after Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev.
But Mr. Pashinyan told Armenians not to believe "that we are doing this for someone else under external pressure".
Mr. Pashinyan — whose party is several seats short of a constitutional majority in Parliament — called on the Opposition not to block the referendum.
"If the people will vote against the constitution, I will resign," he said.
"If they will vote for it, then I will not run for Prime Minister in the next elections," he added.
Mr. Pashinyan, who came to power on the back of mass protests in 2018, has said Armenia's current constitution is linked to the "oligarchy" of previous authoritarian authorities.

India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026).

articles.title: Testing times: On India’s two-Test series against New Zealand
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India needs to be at its best in Tests against New Zealand

New Zealand at home remains an indomitable cricketing opposition. Even the great West Indian squad led by Clive Lloyd suffered a 0-1 Test series defeat in 1980. Pitches that look lush as English meadows, the wind that is often bone-chilling cold, and fast bowlers relishing their prospects, make any tour of New Zealand a difficult outing. So far, the visiting Indians have done well, having won the T20I and ODI series, but the real contest starts with the first Test at Wellington’s Basin Reserve from Thursday. The Shubman Gill-led men’s last overseas tour of Sri Lanka ended with a middling 1-0 victory in the two Tests, but more needs to be done against New Zealand in the latest two-Test series. Placed fourth in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) table, and with hopes of securing a final berth seemingly fragile, India is in a win-all-games situation first up against New Zealand and later when Australia arrives next year. Against current WTC topper New Zealand, the Indian batters have to stay anchored. This is a line-up that no longer has Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane. Gill and company get another opportunity to reiterate their credentials.

For some rugged inspiration they need not look beyond coach Gautam Gambhir in their dressing room. The doughty former India opener batted for 643 minutes while scoring a match-saving 137 in the Napier Test during the 2009 tour. The southpaw will be hoping that the current batting unit, which is high on flair, will remain sober and effectively counter the host. K.L. Rahul, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Devdutt Padikkal and Gill have the onerous task of negating the New Zealand seamers in their backyard. Rishabh Pant and Dhruv Jurel add depth, and if the former can successfully unleash his maverick batting approach, India can upset the host’s best-laid plans. New Zealand will miss the retired Kane Williamson but its batters would be comfortable on familiar surfaces. For India, much would hinge on how Jasprit Bumrah bowls. If the spearhead clicks, then it becomes easier for much of his support-cast that includes the persevering Mohammed Siraj, who was a touch rusty in Sri Lanka. From the squads of the past to the present unit, Ravindra Jadeja remains the link. Whether he will get a role to play or whether the management prefers an all-pace attack, remains a matter of conjecture. The home team led by Tom Latham will depend on Matt Henry, Kyle Jameson and other pacers, to choke the Indian batters. A hard task awaits India, first at Wellington and then at Christchurch.

articles.title: Many imperatives: On India’s Asia diplomacy
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Descriptive Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: India must shore up its partnerships in the Asian region

Each year, the summits of the 11-member Association of South-East Asian Nations mark an important moment on the diplomatic calendar: India is able to interact with all of its partners in the Indo-Pacific and engage global powers at the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s talks with Indo-Pacific players focused on a future shaped “not by competition, but by cooperation”. This year, the summit in Manila hosted by the Philippines had many other imperatives. These were the first ASEAN summits since the U.S.-Israel attacks on Iran and Iran’s Hormuz blockade and strikes on Gulf countries that have upended energy and trade across South and South East Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for “peace, stability, and predictability” in the world during the EAS was aimed as much at leaders from the U.S., Russia and China as it was for the region. The visit had a bilateral context — the Philippines and India have intensified ties considerably in the past year, since the visit of President Bongbong Marcos to Delhi in August 2025, including the upgradation of the Strategic Partnership, maritime exchanges and negotiations over the supply of more Indian-made Brahmos missile battery systems to the Philippines. This year, after months of concerns about U.S. President Donald Trump’s lack of interest in the Quad grouping, the U.S. decided to host a summit of U.S.-India-Australia-Japan Quad leaders on the side-lines of the ASEAN summits, the first time the summit has been held in a non-Quad country.

Given the stakes, there were several outcomes from all the three summits that PM Modi attended back-to-back on Tuesday — the ASEAN India Summit launched a new cooperation on disaster management, and the East Asia Summit focused on countering cyber-crime. PM Modi’s announcement that India would give all ASEAN citizens free tourist visas is expected to increase people-to-people interactions and trade. At the Quad summit, President Trump made a number of announcements including the launch of a Quad Business leaders forum, to be held in Mumbai next year, and the first Quad naval exercises with patrol aircraft. However, the outcomes in Manila paled in significance to the anticipation over Mr. Trump’s next stop in Shenzhen for the Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC), with an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping planned on Thursday. New Delhi must watch the outcomes of that summit among the “global superpowers” much more closely.

Constitutional & Policy Analysis: A critical evaluation of recent executive and judicial developments highlights the need for transparent implementation, federal cooperation, and statutory accountability across central and state institutions.

articles.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences.

articles.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday.

Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments.

He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit.

The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance.
Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said.

He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet.
After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent.

The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. The legislation aimed to attract foreign universities to Tamil Nadu and provide students access to international-standard educational facilities within the State.
Lok Sabha MP C. Robert Bruce and Rajya Sabha MP Christopher Tilak were present.

articles.title: Gandhi is the core ideological enemy of the Sangh Parivar: Ramachandra Guha
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Indian Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Government Schemes
fullParagraphs: While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi.

“When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan.

Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress.

“Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. You can think of no other thinker; he catches so many vital aspects of our lives,” Dr. Guha observed, as the conversation veered towards his ideas of non-violent science which influenced several scientists, including J.B.S. Haldane and Laurie Baker. Gandhi, he said, derived his principles from all traditions and belief systems – Jainism, Vaishnavism, Christianity, and even communism. His attitude to gender, religion, or non-violence evolved through his engagements with various philosophies.

“I do not see him as a quintessentially Hindu thinker, quintessentially Indian thinker, [or] quintessentially traditional thinker. He transcends these lanes. Or Leftist, Rightist, Conservative; he is all three,” Dr. Guha added.

On the question of caste and the equations with the Ambedkarite principles, Dr. Guha said that Gandhi was a guilt-ridden upper caste while Ambedkar was a dalit without emancipation and they could only take those paths. From the perspective of history and the future of India, the paths are converging. Asked if Gandhi’s methods are lost in the era of social media, he said the “cockroaches showed that they have it”. If the book came out a few months later, he said he would have added a few paragraphs on the Cockroach Janata Party movement.
